name: Swashbuckler Dedication
chooses: other (a swashbuckler style — the class's subclass option)
restriction: The six options are exactly d.classes.swashbuckler.subclass.options; the dedication grants ONLY the style's bravado-action tagging, not its granted feat or skill ('You don't gain any other effects of your chosen style').
effect: Sets which actions gain the bravado trait (panache generation) and, second-order, which skill the trained-in grant offers: Acrobatics OR the style's skill; if already trained in both, any skill instead.
evidence: "Choose a swashbuckler's style. ... You become trained in Acrobatics or the skill associated with your style. If you were already trained in both skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) No style pick exists at all — the feat has no `choice`. (2) The skill grant is currently WRONG: featGrantsAuto.ts has `'swashbuckler-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }`, which unconditionally offers ANY skill instead of Acrobatics-or-style-skill-with-fallback. FeatGrant.skillChoices takes a STATIC options list, so the style-dependent option set can only be expressed via FeatGrant.choiceGrants keyed by the style value (each style entry = skillChoices [acrobatics, <styleSkill>] + redundantFallback) — verify choiceGrants is honoured for skillChoices/redundantFallback, or add a dependent-choice lane.

name: Settlement Scholastics
chooses: language (plus a free-text settlement name that becomes the Lore subject)
openSource: core.json `languages` collection (120 entries), restricted to common or uncommon rarity
restriction: Must be a language 'prevalent in that settlement' — GM-adjudicated, so the pool cannot be narrowed mechanically; offer all common/uncommon languages.
effect: Adds one known language. The Lore half is already covered: featFeatGrants.ts maps this feat → 'additional-lore', whose FEAT_GRANTS entry is { loreChoices: 1 }, giving the free-text 'Lore skill for that settlement' pick. Only the language is missing.
evidence: "Choose a specific settlement. You gain the Additional Lore skill feat in the Lore skill for that settlement and learn a single common or uncommon language of your choice that's prevalent in that settlement."
engineNote: There is NO feat→language lane. FeatGrant (src/rules/featGrants.ts) has no `languages` field; Character.languages is built only from ancestry.languages.granted + max(0,Int mod)+ancestry.additional chosen slots (build.ts ~2790). Needs FeatGrant.languages / a language-pick slot merged into Character.languages. Second issue: maxTakable is null (repeatable, 'choose a different settlement'), and both featLoreChoices and featSkillChoices are keyed `<featId>:<index>` with no per-TAKE index — repeat takes will collide unless the key includes the take ordinal.

name: Cavalier Dedication
openSource: core.json `animalCompanions` — the ~40 entries whose special ability list includes 'mount' (beetle, draft-lizard, horse, riding-drake, aon-elephant, …)
restriction: Must have the mount special ability AND be at least one size larger than the character (a Small-starting animal may begin Medium, changing only its size). Additional options 'from your pledge' are GM-approved and cannot be enumerated.
effect: Grants a young animal companion that serves as your mount.
evidence: "You gain a young animal companion that serves as your mount. You can choose from animal companions with the mount special ability ... You must choose an animal companion that's at least one size larger than you"
engineNote: The PICK already exists — companionGrants.ts has `'cavalier-dedication': { kind: 'animal', label: 'Cavalier Dedication', note: 'Grants an animal companion — choose its type and advance it in the Edit tab.' }` — so this needs no new `choice` field. What's missing is the RESTRICTION: CompanionGrant has no filter, so the picker offers all 98 animal companions including non-mounts. Add an optional filter (e.g. requiresAbility: 'mount' + size-vs-character check) to CompanionGrant and honour it in the Companions picker.

name: Eldritch Archer Dedication
prompt: Cantrip (must require a spell attack roll)
chooses: cantrip (and, implicitly, the tradition it comes from)
openSource: core.json `spells` filtered to rank 0, tradition ∈ {arcane, divine, occult, primal}, common rarity — i.e. the existing SpellChoiceFilter { traditions: [...4], cantripsOnly: true }
restriction: The cantrip MUST require a spell attack roll, and the chosen tradition then fixes the tradition of the granted repertoire.
effect: Grants a spontaneous spell repertoire containing that one cantrip; trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC; key spellcasting attribute Charisma. Only applies if the character doesn't already cast from spell slots.
evidence: "You gain a spell repertoire with one cantrip of your choice, from a tradition of your choice. ... This cantrip must require a spell attack roll and come from your chosen tradition."
engineNote: Use the existing lane — effectChoices[].spellFilter (25 feats already do: minor-magic, otherworldly-acumen, …) — NOT the `choice` field. Two gaps: (1) SpellChoiceFilter has no way to say 'requires a spell attack roll' (fields are traditions/rank/minRank/maxRank/traits/cantripsOnly) — needs a `requiresSpellAttack` predicate or the importer must tag attack-roll spells. (2) The record also carries no `spellcastingGrant`, so 'trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC, key attribute Charisma' currently does nothing; spellcastingGrant needs a tradition, which here is derived from the picked cantrip rather than being static.
question: Should the granted cantrip be delivered through the innate lane (like Minor Magic's grantAs:'innate' at-will) or as a real one-cantrip SPONTANEOUS repertoire with a Charisma-keyed spell attack/DC? The text says repertoire, and later Eldritch Archer feats add to it — but the innate lane is the one that exists today.

name: Magic Ammunition
openSource: core.json `items` — magical ammunition of level ≤ 4, common rarity (bane-ammunition, elemental-ammunition, shining-ammunition, vine-arrow, antler-arrow, sleep-arrow, ranging-shot, beacon-shot, …)
restriction: Common, magical, ammunition, 4th level or lower. The GM may extend this to uncommon or other-book ammunition — allow an override rather than hard-blocking.
effect: Defines the menu the Transform Ammunition action can convert your ammunition into. Pure record-keeping — no stat changes on the sheet.
evidence: "When you select this feat, choose three types of common magical ammunition of 4th level or lower from *GM Core* or this book." plus "**Special** You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, select three additional types of magical ammunition"
engineNote: Two problems. (1) No multi-pick open item picker exists for feats (`choice` is a single value; effectChoices/spellFilter only covers spells). (2) DATA GAP: the pool is not expressible from core.json today — items.category === 'ammunition' matches only 3 firearm/air-repeater entries; every magical arrow/bolt/bullet (vine-arrow, shining-ammunition, …) has itemType 'equipment' and category undefined, so ammunition can only be found by name-matching. Also repeatable (maxTakable null), so the pick key must include the take ordinal.
question: For the ammunition pool: add an `ammunition` category/tag in the importer (fixes the data properly for all consumers), or ship a hand-curated id list for this feat only?

name: Terrain Scout
restriction: Two DIFFERENT terrains, from Terrain Stalker's own option list. If the character already has Terrain Stalker, the overlap needs resolving (each Terrain Stalker take must be a different terrain).
effect: Grants the Terrain Stalker skill feat twice, once per chosen terrain. (The 'choose one of those allies' clause is separate and in-play.)
evidence: "You gain the Terrain Stalker skill feat twice, choosing a different terrain each time."
engineNote: featFeatGrants.ts currently has `'terrain-scout': ['terrain-stalker']` — ONE instance, so only one terrain can ever be chosen. terrain-stalker itself already carries the right choice { flag:'choice', kind:'array', options: rubble/snow/underbrush }, but build.ts stores granted-feat picks in `b.grantedFeatChoices[f.featId]` — keyed by featId alone — so a second instance of the same granted feat has nowhere to store its value. Needs the granted-feat list to support a repeated entry with an instance index (and the builder to render two pickers, cross-excluded). Known item: this is on the deferred 'bespoke remainder' list.

name: Elemental Spark
chooses: element (and the versatile damage type it confers)
restriction: Access is Tian Xia origin; a kineticist / elemental sorcerer / non-suli geniekin also has access but MUST take their matching element (hydrokineticist → water, ardande → wood). The builder can offer all five and surface the restriction as a note.
effect: Modifies the Sprite's Spark unarmed attack this feat requires: range 20 ft → 30 ft, and it gains versatile <type> (plus the element's trait when dealing that type).
evidence: "Choose one of the elements below. Your sprite's spark gains the versatile trait, allowing you to choose a different damage type when attacking with it." (prerequisite: Sprite's Spark)
engineNote: There is no lane for ALTERING another record's granted strike. sprites-spark carries `grantedStrikes` (10 heritage-keyed d4 sling-group ranged attacks, range 20). FEAT_CHOICE_STRIKES in build.ts only ADDS a new melee natural attack keyed featId→choiceValue (one entry: iruxi-armaments), so it cannot bump the existing strike's range or append a versatile-<type> trait. Needs a strike-modification lane (target strike by source feat + heritage, patch range/traits).

name: Samsaran Weapon Memory
prompt: Ancestry weapons (choose 2, from two different ancestries)
openSource: core.json `items` where itemType === 'weapon' and traits include an ancestry trait (72 such weapons: dogslicer, clan-pistol, gill-hook, fighting-stick, thunder-sling, …)
restriction: The two weapons must carry ancestry traits from TWO DIFFERENT common humanoid ancestries (or ancestries you have access to). Specific magic weapons that happen to carry an ancestry trait (axe-of-the-dwarven-lords, morning-glow) should be excluded — only base weapons.
effect: Grants access to both weapons and familiarity: martial ones count as simple, advanced ones count as martial for proficiency. At 5th level, critical hits with them apply the weapon's critical specialization effect.
evidence: "Choose two weapons with an ancestry trait from two different common humanoid ancestries ... you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons."
engineNote: CONCRETE LIVE BUG: the record's critSpecWeapons is `{ bases: ['{item|flags.system.rulesSelections.weaponOne}', '{item|flags.system.rulesSelections.weaponTwo}'] }` — unresolved Foundry placeholders. In derive.ts weaponMatches(), a non-empty `bases` sets narrowed=true and no real weapon slug ever equals those strings, so the crit-spec grant is dead for every character. Engine gaps: (a) `choice` is a SINGLE value — two picks need a multi-pick shape; (b) FeatGrant.weaponFamiliarity takes a STATIC `weapons: string[]` and there is no path from a player's pick into it or into critSpecWeapons.bases; (c) the 'two different ancestries' cross-constraint needs picker validation.

name: Inherit the Dreaming Heirloom
prompt: Pusaka Lore subjects (one profession, one environment)
chooses: skill (two Lore subjects, free text) — plus a separate inventory designation of the pusaka item
openSource: Free-text Lore subjects (same input as FeatGrant.loreChoices / Background trainedLoreChoice). Slot 1 = a profession Lore (e.g. Accounting Lore), slot 2 = an environment Lore (e.g. Forest Lore).
restriction: Explicitly permanent: 'Once you make your choice of Lore skills, they can't be changed.' The pusaka itself must be an item of light Bulk that you keep in reach when you sleep.
effect: When you Activate the pusaka (Ancestral Recollection, once per day) you Recall Knowledge with one of these two Lores, becoming TEMPORARILY trained for that check only. You are not otherwise trained in them.
evidence: "select one Lore skill about a profession and one about a type of environment, such as Accounting Lore and Forest Lore ... (you become temporarily trained in these skills for this check). Once you make your choice of Lore skills, they can't be changed."
engineNote: The existing free-text lane (FeatGrant.loreChoices → `lore:<subject>` TRAINED) is mechanically wrong here — the feat grants only per-check temporary training. Needs either a 'recorded, untrained' lore-note lane or an explicit temporary-training marker. Two further gaps outside the choice: (a) 'Choose one item of light Bulk to be your pusaka' is an inventory designation with a real effect (that item becomes a magic item with the occult trait) and there is no item-designation lane; (b) the Guide My Dreams activation casts Guidance as an occult cantrip heightened to half your level, but the record has no `innateSpells`, so it does nothing.
question: For the two pusaka Lores, do we (a) grant them as real trained Lores via loreChoices — simple, reuses an existing lane, but overstates the feat — or (b) add a record-only 'chosen but untrained' lore lane so the sheet shows them without a proficiency?

name: Natural Mutagen
openSource: core.json `items` where traits include 'mutagen', level === 1, rarity === 'common' (bestial, bendy-arm, cognitive, deadweight, drakeheart, energy, juggernaut, quicksilver, sanguine, serene, silvertongue, theatrical)
restriction: Common and 1st level at selection. Excludes the uncommon (war-blood) and rare (prey) mutagens.
effect: Each day during daily preparations you make one free temporary vial of that mutagen; it dissipates by your next preparations. It auto-upgrades to the higher-level version of the same mutagen (moderate, greater, major) as soon as your level reaches that version's level.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, select a common 1st-level mutagen. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make one temporary vial of the selected mutagen. ... your mutagen automatically becomes this higher-level version when your level equals the mutagen's level."
engineNote: No 'free daily consumable' lane exists — the pick has to materialize a temporary item in the inventory at daily prep (closest existing model: the alchemist Advanced Alchemy prep / PlayState.alchemyPrep). The auto-upgrade also needs a mutagen FAMILY ladder (lesser→moderate→greater→major) which core.json does not encode; the versions are separate item ids with no family link.
question: core.json holds duplicate records for every level-1 mutagen — e.g. both `bestial-mutagen` and `bestial-mutagen-lesser` at level 1. Which id set should the picker offer (and is the un-suffixed one a data duplicate that should be deduped)?

name: Signature Weapon
chooses: weapon (plus a free-text name for it)
openSource: core.json `items` where itemType === 'weapon' — ideally narrowed to weapons the character actually owns, since it is a specific physical weapon
restriction: One specific weapon instance. It gains the unique trait; if destroyed, it can be replaced after three days and nights (a re-pick, not an extra pick).
effect: You gain that weapon's critical specialization effect, and can summon it to an empty hand with a 1-action occult teleportation effect (within 1 mile, unattended).
evidence: "Pick a weapon and give it a name; this weapon gains the unique trait. You gain access to its critical specialization effect."
engineNote: CONCRETE LIVE BUG in the other direction from samsaran-weapon-memory: this record has `critSpec: true` with NO `critSpecWeapons`. In derive.ts weaponMatches(), `if (!w) return true` — so the sheet currently shows critical specialization on EVERY strike the character makes, instead of on the one picked weapon. The fix needs a path from the player's pick into critSpecWeapons.bases (that field is static data today; no choice-driven resolution exists). The free-text weapon name is cosmetic and can ride on the inventory item's custom name.

name: Relinquish Control
openSource: content.apparition — the 14 animist apparitions in core.json (same option ids as the animist class's `apparition` extraChoices group)
restriction: An apparition you have access to; once picked it is permanent ("you must always choose that apparition").
effect: Locks the chosen apparition into the character's daily attunement set — i.e. the builder must force this id to be one of build.extraChoices['apparition'] at every level, and it can no longer be swapped out.
evidence: "**Special** This feat requires a particularly strong bond with a specific apparition to learn. Choose one apparition you have access to; once you learn this feat, you must always choose that apparition as one of the apparitions you attune to each day."
engineNote: FeatChoiceDef has no kind that resolves options from another content collection (only 'array' and 'domains'), so this needs either a new kind (e.g. 'apparitions') or an explicit 14-option array. Beyond the picker, the real work is the CONSTRAINT: a feat choice that pins one slot of a class extraChoices group. No such feat→extraChoices coupling exists today. The rest of the feat (+4 status to saves vs controlled, +2 circumstance to Lore Recall Knowledge, restricted action list) is a conditional in-play buff and needs no lane.

name: Cutting Without Blade
prompt: Ikon feat gained for the day
openSource: Feats with the `ikon` trait of level 16 or lower that you don't already have (27 ikon feats exist in core.json; 8+ are level ≤6)
restriction: Ikon trait, level ≤ 16, re-chosen at each daily preparation
effect: The character temporarily gains that ikon feat and all of its effects for the day.
evidence: "Each day during your daily preparations, you can select one ikon feat of 16th level or lower and gain it temporarily for that day."
question: A daily-swappable temporary feat: model it as a fixed builder pick (FEAT_PICK_GRANTS entry, player retrains when they want a different one) or as a play-state daily-prep slot like Advanced Alchemy? I can specify either, but which one is your call.
engineNote: The PICKING half already has an exact-fit lane: FEAT_PICK_GRANTS in src/rules/featPickGrants.ts would take { prompt, category: 'class', traits: ['ikon'], maxLevel: 16 } and the builder SubCard picker + effect application come for free. What has no lane is (a) re-selection at each daily prep rather than at build, and (b) the feat's OTHER clause — "Any ikon feats you've taken now apply to any applicable ikon you have, not just one" — which removes the per-ikon binding of every ikon feat the character owns; there is no ikon-binding model to relax, so that half is prose-only.

name: Animist Dedication
openSource: content.apparition — the 14 animist apparitions in core.json
restriction: "a single apparition from those available to the animist"; changing it costs 1 day of downtime (a retrain, not a per-day swap)
effect: You attune to that apparition each day: trained in its two apparition skills (both are Lores — e.g. Crafter in the Vault → Architecture Lore, Engineering Lore), rising to expert at 8th and master at 16th while attuned; its listed cantrip is added to the cantrips you may prepare.
evidence: "Choose a single apparition from those available to the animist. You become bound to that apparition and can attune to it each day during your daily preparations to become trained in its apparition skills. If you are 8th level, you are expert in its apparition skills while attuned to it, and if you are 16th level, you are a master ..."
engineNote: The CASTING half is already handled — casterArchetypes.ts has 'animist-dedication': mk('divine', 'wis', 2, 'animist'), which covers the 2 divine cantrips + trained spell attack/DC. What is missing is the apparition itself: build.ts only ever reads apparitions from the animist CLASS's extraChoices group ('apparition', pickByLevel 1:2 / 7:3 / 15:4), so an archetype character has no apparition at all. Needed: (1) an option source for apparitions on a feat choice (FeatChoiceDef only knows 'array' and 'domains' today); (2) a level-scaling skill grant — trained→expert@8→master@16 on the two Lore skills the picked apparition names (its `apparitionSkills`; note the existing skillChoices lane has a rankUpgrade { level, rank } shape that covers only ONE upgrade step, so two steps need an extension); (3) the apparition's cantrip added to the archetype's preparable list.

name: Patron Reborn
openSource: content.patron — the 16 witch patrons in core.json (the record's own descRefs point at 'the-resentment' and 'starless-shadow', both present)
restriction: one patron type, fixed when the feat is taken
effect: Nothing on your own sheet: it decides WHICH allied witches automatically count as your Witch's Charge. Record/display only.
evidence: "You can be a patron for other witches. Choose a single type of patron you represent, such as The Resentment or Starless Shadow. An allied witch you can observe who has that patron counts as and gains the benefits of your Witch's Charge feat"
question: Should the builder prompt for picks that provably do nothing to the owning character (this one only changes which ALLIES benefit)? If yes I'd wire it as a store-and-display choice; if no, this record needs nothing.
engineNote: No engine work for the choice itself — it is a stored string shown on the feat entry. The feat's self-affecting parts are already in the data (senses: darkvision + truesight).

name: Mythic Magic
prompt: Spells you can cast with Mythic Magic
openSource: Any spell of 1st or 2nd rank (SpellChoiceFilter { minRank: 1, maxRank: 2 }); plus one 3rd-rank spell unlocked at 14th level and one 4th-rank spell at 20th (the filter's existing minLevel field covers both)
restriction: "take no more than 3 actions to cast and that are either instantaneous or have a duration of 10 minutes or less" — SpellChoiceFilter has NO action-cost and NO duration field, so this restriction cannot be machine-enforced; the picker would be permissive and the restriction shown as picker help text.
effect: Each picked spell becomes castable by spending a Mythic Point, at its normal action cost, automatically heightened to a rank equal to half your level (rounded up), using mythic proficiency for spell attack rolls and DC. If you are not otherwise a caster the attribute is Charisma; otherwise your spellcasting class's attribute.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose up to three spells of 1st or 2nd rank ... **Special** At 14th level, add one spell of 3rd rank for you to cast using this ability. At 20th level, add one 4th-rank spell."
engineNote: The PICKING half fits the existing filtered-spell lane exactly: five EffectChoice entries with spellFilter — three of { minRank: 1, maxRank: 2, grantAs: 'innate' }, one { rank: 3, minLevel: 14 }, one { rank: 4, minLevel: 20 }. Three things have no lane: (a) the cast COST is a Mythic Point, not a uses/day cadence (InnateSpellGrant only models uses); (b) auto-heighten to half level rounded up (heighten fields exist but not a level-derived formula); (c) mythic proficiency for the attack/DC. Also note "up to three" — the picks are optional, so the builder must not block completion on empty slots.

name: Marshall Fiendish Forces
openSource: A common fiend of level 11 or lower (level 15 or lower at 20th level). PROBLEM: core.json ships no creature/bestiary collection at all — the pool does not exist in the builder's data (the tracker's separate public/data scrape is not loaded by the sheet).
restriction: common rarity, fiend trait, level ≤ 11 (≤ 15 at 20th level)
effect: When you Manifest your Realm the chosen fiend appears as a minion for the duration.
evidence: "This fiend is a common fiend of level 11 or lower, which you select when you take this feat. ... At 20th level, you can choose a common fiend of level 15 or lower to appear instead"
question: There is no bestiary in core.json, so this pick has nothing to pick from. Free-text field (player types the fiend's name), or leave the feat prose-only until creature data ships?
engineNote: Even with a list, a summoned minion has no home: the companions lane (CompanionConfig) is for animal companions/familiars/eidolons/vehicles, not arbitrary statblocks. I would not invent a field for this.

name: Beast Lord Dedication
chooses: other (one of the character's own companions)
openSource: The character's OWN companions (Character.companions) — filtered to those that satisfied the prerequisite: a mature (or better) animal companion, or an advanced construct companion
restriction: "a companion that qualified you for this feat" — mature animal companion or advanced construct companion. If the character has exactly one qualifying companion the pick is forced and can be auto-resolved without a prompt.
effect: That companion's Intelligence modifier rises to +0 (or by 1 if already above +0); it understands and can speak a language you know (only you understand it); and while both are conscious within 30 feet, you and it both roll saves against mental effects and the best result is used.
evidence: "Choose a companion that qualified you for this feat as your united companion. Your united companion increases its Intelligence modifier to +0 or by 1 if its Intelligence modifier is greater than +0."
engineNote: Three gaps: (1) no choice lane resolves options from the character's own companions list — every existing option source is a content collection; (2) CompanionConfig has no ability-modifier field for animal/construct companions (only eidolon carries its own mods, in EidolonConfig), so the Int bump has nowhere to land; (3) the shared best-of mental save is a cross-actor rule with no representation. The language grant could ride the existing grantsLanguages lane only if it targeted the PC — it does not, it targets the companion.

name: Godling Dedication
restriction: decided once, when you gain the feat
effect: Sets the key attribute for the archetype's spell attack modifier and spell DC (and, per the last paragraph, the attribute your hierophant uses too).
evidence: "You gain expert proficiency in spell modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is your choice of Wisdom or Charisma, decided when you gain this feat."
engineNote: The DOMAIN half of this feat is already done — effectChoices[0] ('domain') enumerates all 44 domains with the correct focusSpells grant, and focusPoolBonus: 1 is set. The gap is the attribute: the record hard-codes spellcastingGrant: { tradition: 'divine', keyAbility: 'wis', proficiency: 'expert' }, so a Charisma godling silently gets the wrong spell DC. SpellcastingGrant is a static object with no choice hook; casterArchetypes.ts already solved the same problem for the psychic with a `choiceKeyAbility?: AbilityId[]` field, so the fix is to mirror that onto SpellcastingGrant (choiceKeyAbility: ['wis','cha']) rather than to add a `choice`. The third "choose" in the text — "choose one willing ally to be your hierophant" — is an NPC/party decision with no sheet effect and needs no prompt.

name: Gird Champion
openSource: Any weapon BASE type — content.items filtered to category 'weapon', keyed by base-item slug (the same key critSpecWeapons.bases already matches, e.g. 'longsword', 'sickle')
restriction: one weapon type, fixed when the feat is taken
effect: You (and your hierophant) treat that weapon as a SIMPLE weapon for proficiency; you gain its critical specialization effect; and Strikes with it deal an extra 1d6 spirit damage (optionally retyped to match a damage type one of your current domain spells can deal).
evidence: "choose one type of weapon with special significance to you, such as a longsword or a sickle. This becomes your favored weapon. You and your hierophant both treat this weapon as a simple weapon for the purposes of proficiency." — and the record already carries the unresolved placeholder: critSpecWeapons: { bases: ["{actor|flags.system.godlingWeapon}"] }
engineNote: This is a live bug, not just a missing prompt: critSpecWeapons.bases contains the literal Foundry actor-flag string "{actor|flags.system.godlingWeapon}", which can never match any weapon slug, so the crit-spec grant is dead. Work needed: (a) resolve critSpecWeapons.bases from the stored pick instead of the placeholder; (b) StrikeDamageRider has no weapon-base restriction (only appliesTo: all/unarmed/melee/ranged), so a naive strikeDamage entry would add 1d6 spirit to EVERY Strike — needs a `bases` restriction on the rider; (c) "treat as a simple weapon for proficiency" needs a per-weapon category override — the weaponOverrides lane used by ancestry weapon-familiarity is the closest existing fit. The optional damage-type swap is a second, DEPENDENT choice (its options are the damage types of the character's own domain spells) — I would leave that prose-only rather than model a dependent picker.

name: Sanctified Relic
restriction: One of the two MUST be your key attribute. A second, separate choice picks holy or unholy sanctification, and is FORCED to match if you already have the holy or unholy trait from a class feature — a cross-record constraint the builder cannot currently validate.
effect: Nothing on your own sheet. The chosen attributes and trait are conferred by an apex item that only your hierophant can wear: "You can't wear this apex item, but your hierophant can."
evidence: "When you take this feat, choose two attributes (one of which must be your key attribute) as your divine attributes and either holy or unholy sanctification; if you have the holy or unholy trait through a class feature or other ability, you must choose that same trait."
question: Same call as Patron Reborn, and it also decides the shape here: prompt for build-time picks that only benefit an NPC hierophant? If yes, do you want this as ONE choice with 2 picks plus a separate holy/unholy choice, or a single flattened option list? FeatChoiceDef has no `picks` count today — every existing use is pick-one.
engineNote: Note for whoever implements: FeatChoiceDef currently expresses exactly one pick (FeatChoice.choice is a single {value,label}); a 2-pick choice needs the shape widened, or two separate choice entries. The regular apex lane (item.apexAttribute) and the ABP apex are untouched by this feat — it grants the apex trait to an item worn by someone else.

name: Assume Godhood
openSource: Any arcane, occult, or primal spell — "any list other than the divine list" maps cleanly onto the existing SpellChoiceFilter.traditions allow-list ['arcane','occult','primal'], so no exclude-filter is needed. Three picks with different rank windows: one { rank: 1 }, one { minRank: 2, maxRank: 3 }, one unbounded.
restriction: one must be 1st rank, one must be 2nd or 3rd rank, one may be any rank; none may be from the divine list
effect: They become additional cleric spells you can grant to your FOLLOWERS. Nothing lands on your own sheet.
evidence: "When you Assume Godhood, choose three spells from any list other than the divine list; one must be 1st rank, one must be 2nd or 3rd rank, and one can be of any rank. These spells become additional cleric spells you can grant to your followers."
question: This feat has THREE separate build-time picks and none of them touch your own sheet — the three follower spells, "one skill you are legendary in to act as your divine skill", and "one other attribute of your choosing" for your divine attributes. Prompt for all of them as record-only, prompt for none, or something in between?
engineNote: If you do model it: the spell picks fit the filtered-spell lane except that grantAs is neither 'innate' nor 'focus' (the spells go to other characters), so a third grant mode — or a no-grant/record-only mode — would be needed. The divine-skill pick is the only one with a machine-checkable restriction ("one skill you are legendary in"), which the conditional-rank skillChoices lane could validate. Also note this feat depends on Godling Dedication and inherits its domain/favored-weapon picks ("you can provide any aspect of a deity stat block ... that you yourself have acquired from a godling feat") — no new choice there.

name: Mental Forge
restriction: Two DIFFERENT traits from the list; changing them costs 1 week of retraining.
evidence: "Choose two of the following weapon traits to give your mind weapon: grapple, modular (B, P, or S), nonlethal, shove, or trip. Once chosen, these weapon traits can't be changed unless you spend 1 week retraining"
effect: The two chosen traits are added to the character's mind weapon permanently.
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) FeatChoiceDef is single-pick (one flag/prompt/kind) — a 2-pick choice needs either a `picks` field or two choice defs, neither of which exists. (2) There is NO mind weapon to attach traits to: core.json items contains no 'Mind Weapon' record (only indomitable-keepsake / lucky-keepsake), and mind-smith-dedication itself carries no choice for its own 1d4-agile-finesse / 1d6-finesse / 1d8 / 1d10-reach statistics. Until the mind weapon exists as a real (virtual) weapon item, this pick has no target.

name: Runic Mind Smithing
restriction: Re-chosen every day during daily preparations; counts against your normal property-rune limit.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one rune from the following list of weapon property runes: corrosive, flaming, frost, shock, thundering, and vitalizing."
effect: Etches the chosen property rune onto the mind weapon until the next daily preparations.
engineNote: All six runes exist as item ids (corrosive, flaming, frost, shock, thundering, vitalizing), so the option values map cleanly. Blockers: (a) same as Mental Forge — no mind weapon item exists to etch onto; (b) this is a DAILY re-selection, and Feat.choice is a permanent build-state field. The app's only daily-prep lane today is the alchemist's Advanced Alchemy prep.
question: Should daily-reselectable picks (Runic Mind Smithing, Malleable Mental Forge, Starstone Aspirant Dedication) live in Feat.choice as a sticky default the player can edit on the sheet, or get a proper daily-preparations lane?

name: Talon's Mark
openSource: An item you own carrying the `tattoo` trait (116 such items exist in core.json: blessed-tattoo, warding-tattoo, familiar-tattoo, …). A mundane/non-magical tattoo is also legal per the feat, and the app has no record for that.
restriction: Requirements line: "You have a magical or mundane tattoo."
evidence: "Choose a tattoo you have. If the tattoo wasn't already a magic item, it becomes a level 6 item with the invested, occult, and tattoo traits. It also gains the Twist Design and Adopt Persona abilities."
effect: The chosen tattoo becomes (or stays) a magic item and gains two activatable abilities — both exist as records: actions['twist-design'] and actions['adopt-persona'].
engineNote: FeatChoiceDef cannot enumerate the character's INVENTORY — it only carries a fixed `options` array. The nearest existing machinery is the inventory-side item targeting used by the Doubling Rings rune-copy picker and the drag-to-attach rune/talisman validator (InventoryTab). This needs an item-targeting choice kind, plus a way to bolt two granted actions onto a chosen inventory item.

name: Starstone Aspirant Dedication
openSource: Any skill (including Lores) in which you are currently UNTRAINED — computed from the character's live proficiencies, not a fixed list.
restriction: Must be a skill you are untrained in; re-chosen each day during daily preparations.
evidence: "Each day during your daily preparations, choose a skill you're untrained in. You can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained in that skill, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks with that skill until your next daily preparations. At 8th level, this bonus increases to +2, and at 15th level, this bonus increases to +3."
effect: Unlocks trained-only skill actions for that skill WITHOUT granting the trained rank, plus a +1/+2/+3 circumstance bonus scaling at levels 1/8/15.
engineNote: Three things the engine cannot express today. (1) No 'skills you are untrained in' option filter — featGrants.skillChoices takes `options: SkillId[] | 'any'` with no current-rank predicate. (2) No numeric skill bonus from a feat: EffectGrant.skills only sets a RANK, and the numeric `skills` map lives on ItemPassiveEffects (item-only). (3) No 'counts as trained for actions but is not trained' concept — granting trained rank instead would be wrong (it would also change the DC-scaling and prerequisite math).
question: Same daily-vs-build question as Runic Mind Smithing. Also: is a Modes entry (+1/+2/+3 circumstance to one chosen skill) an acceptable stand-in, or do you want a real feat-level numeric skill-bonus lane?

name: Mortal Possibility
openSource: Any skill in which the character is ALREADY master — computed live from proficiencies (at 20th level that is typically a small set).
restriction: Must already be master in the chosen skill.
evidence: "Choose a skill you have master proficiency in. You become legendary in that skill. In addition, you gain a skill feat of your choice for that skill."
effect: Raises the chosen skill to legendary, and grants one bonus skill feat that must be a feat for that same skill. (The once-a-day +3 status bonus is play-time bookkeeping.)
engineNote: Partially expressible, but not safely. featGrants.skillChoices supports `{options:'any', rank:'legendary'}`, but there is NO minimum-current-rank predicate — with 'any' the player could pick an untrained skill and jump straight to legendary, which is wrong (grants RAISE only, so nothing stops it). featGrants.bonusSkillFeat exists but injects an UNRESTRICTED skill-feat slot; there is no way to say 'a skill feat for the skill you just picked'. Both need engine work. The trailing 'first time each day you succeed... +3 status bonus to your next check within the hour' has no lane at all and should stay prose.

name: Breakthrough Innovation
restriction: Must match your innovation's TYPE (armor / construct / weapon); several options carry their own extra prerequisite (Camouflage Pigmentation = subterfuge suit only; Heavy Construction = power suit only; Hyper Boosters requires speed boosters; Marvelous Gears requires wonder gears; Turret Configuration requires projectile launcher; Advanced Rangefinder / Rope Shot = ranged only; Aerodynamic Construction / Inconspicuous Appearance = melee only; Integrated Gauntlet = one-handed non-two-hand; Tangle Line = thrown only). An initial modification of the same type may be taken instead.
evidence: "Choose a breakthrough modification of your innovation's type to apply to your innovation. You can choose an initial modification of your innovation's type instead if you prefer."
effect: Applies one modification's effect (resistances, AC/save bonuses vs spells, speed bonuses, added weapon traits, construct-companion upgrades).
engineNote: classFeatures already support `effectChoices` (13 records use them), so the MENU is expressible — but three gaps remain. (1) The option list must be FILTERED by the chosen innovation subclass; there is no conditional-options mechanism on EffectChoice, so all 21 would be offered to everyone. (2) 'or an initial modification instead' widens the pool to records not enumerated here, and inventor modifications have no `initial vs breakthrough` tagging anywhere. (3) The 6 CONSTRUCT modification records do NOT exist in core.json (advanced-weaponry, antimagic-construction, climbing-limbs, durable-construction, marvelous-gears, turret-configuration are all missing), while the 8 armor and 7 weapon ones DO exist as classFeatures — so a construct inventor's options are unresolvable references today. Several effects (resistance = half level, +1 circumstance vs spells, added weapon traits) also have no grant lane.
question: Should the picker offer breakthrough modifications only, or breakthrough + initial as the text allows? And which innovation type does light-mortar-innovation count as for this filter — weapon?

name: Offensive Boost
restriction: Swappable with downtime, the same way modifications are switched.
evidence: "Choose one of the following boosts, with the damage type in parentheses." — "Your improvements make any Strikes that rely on your innovation deal an additional 1d6 damage, with a type determined by the boost you choose."
effect: +1d6 damage of the chosen type on innovation-dependent Strikes (weapon innovation: your innovation's Strikes; construct: the companion's Strikes; armor: your melee unarmed Strikes plus one weapon chosen daily).
engineNote: The MENU fits `effectChoices` on a classFeature (13 already do), but the EFFECT does not: EffectGrant has no 'extra damage dice on Strikes' field at all, so the pick can be stored and displayed but will not reach the strike-damage breakdown. The armor-innovation branch also carries a SECOND, daily choice — "one weapon you choose during daily preparations" — which is a per-day inventory-weapon pick with no lane (the record's own trailing note flags this: "the included effect is only needed for construct innovations and armor innovations for selecting their daily preparation weapon").

name: Irezoko Tattoo
chooses: other (one of your own classes that has a focus pool)
openSource: the character's own class(es) that grant access to a focus pool — normally exactly one, two under the Dual Class variant rule
restriction: Must be a class you are a member of AND that grants you a focus pool.
evidence: "Choose a class that you are a member of that grants you access to a focus pool. When you take this feat, it gains the trait that applies to your chosen class."
effect: Two things: (a) the feat itself gains the chosen class's trait (which is what makes it legal in that class's feat slots / archetype interactions), and (b) unlocks a once-per-day three-action activity to recover 1 Focus Point.
engineNote: NEEDS ENGINE WORK on both halves. (1) Option source: FeatChoiceDef.kind only has 'array' (static list) and 'domains' (resolved from the deity). There is no kind that resolves options from the character's classes, so this cannot be authored today without hard-coding all 27 class ids as an 'array' — which would let the player pick a class they don't have. (2) Effect: there is no lane that adds a TRAIT to a feat at build time, and no lane for a once/day focus-point-recovery play resource (focusSpells/focusPoolBonus add pool size, not a refill action). Without both, the pick would be display-only.
question: For a single-class character the pick is forced (one option). Should the builder still prompt and record it, auto-resolve silently, or hide the feat when the character has no focus-pool class? And is a once-per-day 'regain 1 Focus Point' worth a real play resource, or a sheet note?

name: Sacred Spells
chooses: other (which of the two flexibility benefits) — and, on the spontaneous branch, 2 spells from a fixed list of 7

options.label: Prepared caster — spend 10 minutes (or while Refocusing) to swap a prepared spell for a same-rank sacred spell
Spontaneous caster with signature spells — add two sacred spells to your repertoire as extra signature spells

restriction: The two options are gated by caster type ('If you're a prepared spellcaster' / 'If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with the signature spells class feature'), so in practice only one is legal per character. The spontaneous branch then needs 2 further picks from: void-warp, death-ward, vitality-lash, infuse-vitality, holy-cascade, magic-stone, sunburst (all 7 ids exist in core.json spells).
evidence: "In addition, your knowledge of the conduits to the Forge of Creation allows you more flexibility with these spells. Choose one of these two benefits."
effect: Prepared branch: a daily-prep swap privilege (no persistent stat). Spontaneous branch: +2 repertoire spells that are also signature spells, re-choosable each time you unlock a new spell rank.
engineNote: NEEDS ENGINE WORK. EffectGrant has no repertoire/signature-spell lane — SpellChoiceFilter.grantAs is only 'innate' | 'focus'. There is also no field for the feat's unconditional first paragraph ('Add Void Warp, Death Ward, … to your spell list'), so even before the choice the feat is inert. With today's shape only a 2-option record-and-display choice is expressible; the 2-of-7 signature picks and the spell-list expansion both need new lanes.

name: Debilitating Venom

options.label: Hampering — Stage 1/2: −5-foot status penalty to Speed; Stage 3: −10-foot
Stumbling — Stage 1: no adjustment; Stage 2: off-guard; Stage 3: off-guard and −5-foot penalty to Speed

restriction: maxTakable is 2; a second take must select the OTHER debilitation. Only one debilitation may be applied to any single use of Envenom.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, select one of the following debilitations. When you use Envenom, you can choose to apply a debilitation to your venom to adjust its effects."
effect: Records which debilitation the character knows, and surfaces it on the sheet next to the Envenom action (Envenom exists in content.actions as id 'envenom'). All the mechanical consequences land on the VICTIM (their Speed, their off-guard condition) at successive venom stages, so nothing on this character's derived stats changes — recording and displaying the pick is the complete, correct outcome.
engineNote: The core pick fits FeatChoiceDef.kind 'array' as-is. One gap worth knowing: FeatChoiceDef has no 'must differ from the previous take' constraint, so with maxTakable 2 a player could pick Hampering twice. Related feat stronger-debilitating-venom (level 13) likely keys off the same pick — worth checking it references the same flag.

name: Primal Dragonblood
openSource: any skill (the replacement when Nature training is redundant)
restriction: Only triggers if the character would already be trained in Nature from another source.
effect: Trained in the chosen skill instead of Nature.
evidence: "If you would automatically become trained in Nature ... you instead become trained in a skill of your choice."
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts has 'primal-dragonblood': { skills: { nature: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }, which fires the skillFallbacks picker. Do NOT add a `choice` field; it would double-prompt. SEPARATE unmodelled constraint: the last sentence ("If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a primal dragon") is a FILTER on an existing picker (BuildState.dragonExemplar for the Draconic bloodline / Dragon Instinct), not a new prompt — no exemplar-filtering lane exists, and core.json's draconicExemplar records carry no primal/imperial classification.

name: Improbable Elixirs
openSource: any item in content.items with the potion trait, item level 9 or lower
restriction: Number of picks = Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). Permanent — "Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed."
effect: Grants formulas to craft those potions as elixir-trait alchemical consumables (alchemist's toolkit/lab substitutes for other toolkits).
evidence: "Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower... Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed."
engineNote: NOT EXPRESSIBLE TODAY. (a) The app has no known-formulas concept at all — I searched all of src/ for `formula`/`knownFormulas`; `formula` only ever means a math expression string (speeds, IWR values). (b) No picker supports a variable pick COUNT driven by an attribute modifier (FeatGrant.skillChoices is a fixed-length array; EffectChoice has no count field). Both are new engine features.
question: Should Heroes Heaven model crafting formulas at all (a new 'Formulas' list on the character), or should Improbable Elixirs just push the chosen potions into the alchemy-prep item list as elixirs? Until formulas exist, the pick has nowhere to land.

name: Auspicious Mount

options.label: Celestial (gains holy; +5 extra HP, weakness 5 to unholy)
Fiend (gains unholy; +5 extra HP, weakness 5 to holy)

restriction: Whichever best matches your deity's servitors (GM/player call; not derivable from core.json's deity records).
effect: Sets the mount's creature trait + holy/unholy trait, its extra-HP tier and its weakness. The OUTER pick (which specialization) rides the companion's existing specialization dropdown.
evidence: "You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization" ... "It gains the celestial, fiend, or monitor trait—whichever best matches your deity's servitors"
engineNote: Two-part. (1) The specialization pick already has a home: CompanionConfig.specialization + content.companionSpecializations (11 entries today). The feat must (a) force the Faithful Steed mount to maturity 'specialized' and (b) ADD a new 'auspice' entry to companionSpecializations — abilityBoosts {int:2, wis:1}, skills [{religion:'expert'}], +20 max HP rising to 25@18 / 30@20, fly Speed = land Speed, plus one bonus language. The Specialization type has no maxHp / speeds / languages / traits fields, so those are new. (2) The celestial/fiend/monitor trait pick is the feat-level `choice` above, and its weakness/extra-HP rider has no companion lane either.

name: Fuse Stance
chooses: other (two stances you already know, plus a free-text name)
openSource: the stances the character already has (feats/features with the stance trait that this character owns — content.stances entries reachable from owned records), NOT the full 128-entry stance list
restriction: Chosen once when the feat is taken and permanent. The GM adjudicates incompatible restrictions.
effect: Creates a single new named stance that, when entered, applies both source stances' effects, attacks, requirements and restrictions at once.
evidence: "When you take this feat, choose two stances you know and combine them into a single fused stance. Give your new fused stance a unique name."
engineNote: NOT EXPRESSIBLE TODAY. The stance manager is deliberately EXCLUSIVE — Character.activeStance is a single stance id and derive injects that one stance's strike/AC/dexCap/speed. A fused stance needs (a) a synthetic stance record composed from two existing ones (merging their derive injections), (b) a free-text name field, and (c) a picker sourced from the character's OWN stances rather than the global list. Also the `choice` shape has no free-text variant (only array/domains) and no 2-pick variant.

name: Domain Acumen
openSource: the domains associated with the character's chosen oracle MYSTERY (not the deity)
restriction: Only domains of your mystery, and only ones you don't already have an initial domain spell from. Repeatable (maxTakable: null) — a different domain each time.
effect: Gain that domain's INITIAL domain spell as a revelation spell, plus the +1 focus point the record already declares (focusPoolBonus: 1).
evidence: "Choose one of the domains associated with your mystery for which you don't already have an initial domain spell. You gain an initial domain spell from that domain"
engineNote: kind 'domains' EXISTS but resolves the wrong source: src/builder/shared.tsx populates it from content.deities[build.deityId].domains, and an oracle has no deity. Needs (a) a new source — a mystery→domains map, because core.json's oracle mystery options carry Related Domains only as prose inside `description` ("**Related Domains** death, duty, family, soul"), with no structured field; and (b) exclusion of domains already picked by an earlier take of this same repeatable feat. The initial-spell lookup itself is already there (DOMAIN_SPELLS in src/rules/domains.ts). Suggest a new kind such as 'mysteryDomains' rather than overloading 'domains'.

name: Domain Fluency
openSource: the domains of your mystery for which you ALREADY have an initial domain spell (i.e. the domains picked by your Domain Acumen takes)
restriction: Requires Domain Acumen; the option list is exactly the set of domains that feat already granted.
effect: Gain that domain's ADVANCED domain spell as a revelation spell, plus the declared focusPoolBonus: 1.
evidence: "Choose one of the domains associated with your mystery for which you have an initial domain spell. You gain an advanced domain spell from that domain"
engineNote: NOT EXPRESSIBLE TODAY, two gaps. (1) src/rules/domains.ts maps domain → INITIAL spell only (DOMAIN_SPELLS, 40-odd entries); there is no ADVANCED_DOMAIN_SPELLS table — one must be authored. (2) The option list depends on ANOTHER feat's picks (Domain Acumen), and no choice kind can read a sibling feat's stored value; the domains resolver would need access to BuildState.featChoices. Same mystery→domains prerequisite as Domain Acumen.

name: Diverse Mystery
openSource: the initial or advanced revelation spell of any oracle mystery OTHER than your own — i.e. classes.oracle subclass options[].focusSpells[0] and options[].advancedFocusSpell for the 10 mysteries you didn't pick (22 candidate spells)
restriction: Not your own mystery; initial or advanced only (never greater). Permanent.
effect: Gain that spell as a revelation (focus) spell. It gains the cursebound trait for you, and casting it also inflicts that mystery's Cursebound 1 effects.
evidence: "Select one revelation spell from a mystery other than your own. You can choose only an initial revelation spell or an advanced revelation spell."
engineNote: Enumerable (22 fixed options) so `choice` kind 'array' would work as data — but the GRANT has no lane on that path: FeatGrant.choiceGrants carries no focusSpells field, and the focus loop in src/rules/build.ts only resolves a feat sub-choice into a spell via DOMAIN_SPELLS. Cheapest route: use `effectChoices` instead of `choice` — EffectChoice.options[].grant is an EffectGrant, which DOES support focusSpells, and buildCharacter already resolves it. The extra Cursebound-on-cast rider has no lane and would be a sheet note.
question: Diverse Mystery has no focusPoolBonus in the record, unlike Domain Acumen/Fluency/Paradoxical Mystery. Is that correct RAW (gain the spell but no extra focus point), or a data omission that should be focusPoolBonus: 1?

name: Arcane Evolution
openSource: any skill
effect: Trained in the chosen skill.
evidence: "You become trained in one skill of your choice."
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts has 'arcane-evolution': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }. Do NOT add a `choice` field; it would double-prompt. The feat's OTHER pick ("During your daily preparations, you can choose one spell in your spell repertoire to be a signature spell that day") is a daily-prep choice, not a build choice — BuildState already stores `signatures` per rank, so an extra daily signature would be a play-layer overlay on that.

name: Occult Evolution
openSource: any skill
effect: Trained in the chosen skill.
evidence: "You become trained in one skill of your choice."
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts has 'occult-evolution': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }. Do NOT add a `choice` field. The second half ("once per day, you can spend 1 minute to choose one mental occult spell you don't know and add it to your spell repertoire") is an explicitly temporary once-per-day pick — play layer, filter = occult spells with the mental trait not already in the repertoire.

name: Greater Crossblooded Evolution
openSource: the `grantedSpells` list of the SECONDARY bloodline chosen with Crossblooded Evolution (classes.sorcerer subclass options[].grantedSpells — 10 spells per bloodline)
restriction: Up to three (fewer is legal). Permanent.
effect: Adds those spells to your repertoire, auto-heightened to the highest rank you can cast (or the highest they can heighten to below that), cast as your PRIMARY bloodline's tradition.
evidence: "Choose up to three of the sorcerous gift spells granted by your secondary bloodline. You add these spells to your spell repertoire"
engineNote: BLOCKED on a missing upstream choice. Its prerequisite, Crossblooded Evolution ("Choose another Bloodline"), is completely unmodelled — I grepped all of src/ for 'crossblooded' and got zero hits — so there is no secondary bloodline to source the option list from. Needs (a) a secondary-bloodline pick on crossblooded-evolution, (b) an option source that reads that pick, (c) a bonus-known-spells lane injecting repertoire entries outside the normal per-rank slots, and (d) 'up to N' (variable-count, may pick fewer) which no existing picker supports.

name: Bloodline Mutation

options.label: Fly Speed equal to your land Speed
Amphibious: breathe water and air, swim Speed equal to your land Speed

restriction: RAW each branch is legal only if the creatures of your bloodline actually fly / are aquatic / have that resistance or immunity. Not derivable from data — see engineNote.
effect: fly → speeds { fly: '@actor.speed.land' }; amphibious → speeds { swim: '@actor.speed.land' } + a water-breathing note; resist-* → resistances [{ type: <energy>, value: 20 }].
evidence: "Choose one of the following." — "you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed" / "you become amphibious ... and you gain a swim Speed" / "choose an energy type your bloodline is immune or resistant to and gain resistance 20 against that energy type"
engineNote: The PICK is expressible today with `effectChoices` (not `choice`): EffectGrant already supports both `speeds` (accepting the '@actor.speed.land' formula string) and `resistances`. Flattening the nested energy sub-choice into six resist-* options avoids needing a two-level picker. NOT expressible: (a) gating the options by which bloodline you took — core.json's bloodline records are bare {id,name} with no creature-trait/IWR data; (b) the unconditional first paragraph ("You gain the appropriate trait or traits" + "low-light vision or darkvision, if one is appropriate"), which is a bloodline-dependent trait/sense grant with no lane.
question: Leave all 8 options always offered (trust-based, with a note that your bloodline must qualify), or hand-author a bloodline→qualifying-options table for the 18 bloodlines?

name: Barbarian Dedication
chooses: other (barbarian instinct — a class subclass option)
restriction: You have the instinct "for all purposes" but gain none of its other abilities; you ARE bound by its anathema.
effect: Satisfies instinct prerequisites (so Basic Fury etc. can grant instinct-gated barbarian feats such as Animalistic Brutality), and applies the instinct's anathema. It must NOT grant the instinct's rage-damage tier.
evidence: "Choose an instinct as you would if you were a barbarian. You have that instinct for all purposes, but you don't gain any of the other abilities it grants."
engineNote: The SKILL half is already done (core.json ships effectChoices 'barbarian-dedication-skill' with 15 skill options). The INSTINCT half is unmodelled: src/rules/derive.ts reads RAGE_DAMAGE[c.subclassId] only when c.classId === 'barbarian', and the archetype branch is a hardcoded flat +2 — correct RAW, and the instinct pick must not change it. Needs an archetype-subclass lane; the precedent already exists (BuildState.archetypeEidolonType stores a summoner subclass option id for Summoner Dedication), so this would be the second such field. Use `choice`/featChoices for storage if the prerequisite validator can read it, otherwise a dedicated BuildState field.

name: Perfection's Path
restriction: Only a save you are already an EXPERT in.
effect: That saving throw's proficiency rank becomes master.
evidence: "Choose one saving throw (Fortitude, Reflex, or Will) in which you are an expert. Your proficiency rank in the chosen saving throw increases to master."
engineNote: FULLY EXPRESSIBLE TODAY — exactly the Canny Acumen pattern: a `choice` (kind 'array') plus FEAT_GRANTS.choiceGrants keyed by the same values, e.g. { fortitude: { save: { fortitude: 'master' } }, reflex: {...}, will: {...} }. choiceGrants keys must match the stored choice value verbatim. Minor caveat: FeatGrant.save RAISES only and there is no conditional-save lane (conditionalSkills exists but is skills-only), so picking a save you're merely trained in would jump you straight to master; the 'expert in at least one saving throw' prerequisite is stored as free text and isn't validated per option. Low-severity over-grant, worth a conditionalSaves lane later.

name: Oracle Dedication
chooses: other (oracle mystery — a class subclass option)
effect: Trained in Religion AND the mystery's own skill (each redundant one converting to a free skill pick), and you gain that mystery's oracular CURSE. It should also be the source for Domain Acumen/Fluency's domain list and for any Basic/Advanced Revelation archetype feats.
evidence: "Choose a Mystery. You become trained in Religion and the mystery's skill; if you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the curse associated with your mystery"
engineNote: Currently only APPROXIMATED: src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts has 'oracle-dedication': { skills: { religion: 'trained' }, skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }], redundantFallback: true } — i.e. the mystery's own skill is collapsed into a generic any-skill pick, and the CURSE is not granted at all. The data needed is present: core.json classes.oracle subclass options carry grants.skills (e.g. ancestors → society) and a Curse of … in descRefs. Needs the same archetype-subclass lane as Barbarian Dedication (precedent: BuildState.archetypeEidolonType), which would then also feed Domain Acumen and Domain Fluency. The spellcasting half is already handled by CASTER_ARCHETYPES['oracle-dedication'].

name: Sorcerer Dedication
chooses: other (sorcerer bloodline — a class subclass option)
restriction: "You don't gain any other abilities from your choice of bloodline" — no blood magic, no bloodline focus spells from the dedication itself.
effect: Trained in the bloodline's TWO skills (each already-trained one converting to a free skill pick), and the bloodline's tradition becomes the archetype's spell tradition and constrains the two cantrips (its list, plus the bloodline's granted spells).
evidence: "Choose a Bloodline. You become trained in the bloodline's two skills; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice."
engineNote: Currently only APPROXIMATED in two places: (1) CASTER_ARCHETYPES marks it choiceTradition: true, so the builder asks the player to pick a TRADITION directly (BuildState.archetypeTradition) instead of deriving it from a bloodline; (2) featGrantsAuto has 'sorcerer-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options:'any', rank:'trained' }, { options:'any', rank:'trained' }] } — two generic free skills instead of the bloodline's two specific skills with a redundancy fallback. The data is present: classes.sorcerer subclass options carry `tradition`, `grants.skills` (2 each) and `grantedSpells`. A real bloodline pick would set tradition + both skills automatically and give Crossblooded Evolution / Greater Crossblooded Evolution and Advanced/Greater Bloodline something to hang off. Same archetype-subclass lane as Barbarian and Oracle Dedication.

name: Blessing of the Devoted
restriction: Champion, level 3. Text also allows "any other to which you have access" — deity/campaign-specific blessings that are not in the shipped data.
effect: Blessed Swiftness: +5-foot status bonus to Speed (and a +2 status bonus to allies' defenses vs reactions triggered in your aura — situational, in-play). Blessed Shield: your held shield gains the Reinforcing rune of your level (minor@3, lesser@7, moderate@10, greater@13, major@16, supreme@19), or +1 Hardness if it already has it. Blessed Armament: a chosen weapon or handwraps of mighty blows gains its critical specialization effect plus one property rune chosen from Fearsome / Ghost Touch / Returning / Shifting / Vitalizing.
evidence: "Your deity blesses your service with a boon. … Choose one of the following blessings, or any other to which you have access."
engineNote: NOT implemented anywhere — champion's class features list has blessing-of-the-devoted at level 3, but no BuildState field, no effectChoices on the record, and no code path mentions it. Shape note: ClassFeature extends ContentBase + DefenseGrants, so the field to add is `effectChoices` (EffectChoice[]: {id, prompt, options:[{value,label,grant?,note?}]}) as gates-threshold already does — NOT the Feat-only `choice`/FeatChoiceDef. Expressibility per option: Blessed Swiftness is nearly expressible via DefenseGrants.landSpeedBonus: 5, except that field is a flat bonus while the text specifies a STATUS bonus (and it redirects to your mount when mounted, which is not modelled). Blessed Armament and Blessed Shield both need a NEW capability: granting a rune / crit-spec to a player-picked inventory ITEM from a class feature, plus Blessed Armament's second nested choice (which rune) and its daily-preparations re-choice. Recommend shipping the three options with grant only on Blessed Swiftness and `note` prose on the other two (the same mixed pattern gates-threshold already uses for its play-time junctions).
question: Blessed Armament / Blessed Shield need item-targeted grants (pick a weapon or handwraps, then pick one of five property runes; or auto-apply a level-scaled Reinforcing rune to your shield) which the engine cannot express today. Ship all three options with only Blessed Swiftness mechanised and the other two as recorded-but-prose picks, or hold the whole feature until an item-targeting lane exists?

name: Divine Access
openSource: any deity in content.deities whose `domains` array intersects your oracle mystery's Related Domains
restriction: Oracle, level 11. Deity must grant one of your mystery's related domains (e.g. Flames mystery → dust, fire, star, sun). A SECOND, dependent choice follows: up to three cleric spells granted by that deity.
effect: Adds up to three of the chosen deity's cleric spells to your spell list, and to your spell repertoire as soon as you can cast spells of the appropriate rank.
evidence: "Choose one deity who grants one of your mystery's granted domains. Add up to three cleric spells of your choice granted by that deity to your spell list, and to your spell repertoire as soon as you can cast spells of the appropriate rank."
engineNote: NOT implemented and BLOCKED ON DATA, twice over. (1) Oracle mystery options (classes.oracle.subclass.options) have keys id/name/description/descRefs/grantedSpells/grants/focusSpells/advancedFocusSpell/greaterFocusSpell — there is NO structured `domains` field; the domains exist only as prose inside the description ("**Related Domains** dust, fire, star, sun"), so the deity filter cannot be computed. (2) Deity records have id/name/traits/rarity/description/source/domains/divineFont/favoredWeapons/skill/edition — there is NO structured deity-spell list; a deity's cleric spells are prose only ("**Cleric Spells** 1st: Breathe Fire, 3rd: Fireball, 4th: Wall of Fire"), so the second pick has no pool. Full fix = extract mystery.domains + deity.clericSpells into core.json, then a two-stage builder control (deity picker filtered by domain overlap, then a 0-3 multi-pick of that deity's spells) feeding the existing rank-gated repertoire-addition lane. This is more than an effectChoices block.
question: Divine Access needs two new structured data fields (oracle mystery → related domains, deity → granted cleric spells) before it can be prompted at all. Do you want those extracted from the existing prose into core.json, or should Divine Access ship as a recorded-but-inert note for now?

name: Implement Adept
openSource: the implements you have already selected — BuildState.extraChoices['implement'] (a dynamic subset of amulet/bell/chalice/lantern/mirror/regalia/shield/tome/wand/weapon)
restriction: Thaumaturge, level 7. Pool is exactly the implements the character owns (2 of them at level 7), so it cannot be a fixed options array.
effect: Grants the adept benefit for the chosen implement — i.e. the corresponding adept-benefit-<implement> classFeature (all ten exist in core.json).
evidence: "You have deepened your connection to one of your implements, unlocking its adept power. Choose one of your implements and gain the adept benefit for that implement."
engineNote: NOT implemented: no BuildState field, no effectChoices on the record, and a full-src search for 'adept' returns nothing implement-related — so the ten adept-benefit-* classFeature records in core.json are currently ORPHANED data, unreachable by any character. Because the option pool is derived from another choice (extraChoices.implement), a static options array cannot express it; this needs a dedicated builder control + BuildState field (e.g. adeptImplements: string[], one entry for this feature and one for `second-adept` at level 11), mirroring how pathToPerfection[] handles the analogous 'choose one you already picked' pattern. Note the sibling feature `second-adept` (level 11) needs the same field with the restriction 'a different implement than the first adept'.

name: Implement Paragon
openSource: the implements you have already selected AND that already gained the adept benefit — the intersection of BuildState.extraChoices['implement'] and the Implement Adept / Second Adept picks
restriction: Thaumaturge, level 17. Must be an implement that already has its adept benefit (so it depends on the Implement Adept and Second Adept picks, not just the implement list).
effect: Grants the paragon benefit for the chosen implement — i.e. the corresponding paragon-benefit-<implement> classFeature (all ten exist in core.json).
evidence: "Choose one of your implements that already gained the adept benefit; you gain the paragon benefit for that implement."
engineNote: NOT implemented, and doubly derived: the pool is a subset of a subset, so it is unrepresentable as a static options array and even depends on a choice (Implement Adept) that itself does not exist yet. The ten paragon-benefit-* records are orphaned data like the adept ones. Fix implement-adept / second-adept first, then this becomes a one-line filtered picker over those picks.

name: Adept Benefit (Wand)
restriction: Must be DIFFERENT from the damage type chosen for the wand's initiate benefit — initiate-benefit-wand says "choose whether your wand is attuned to cold, electricity, or fire". So the live pool is the two types not already taken.
effect: Fling Magic's range increases to 120 feet, and each time you Fling Magic you may pick either of your two chosen damage types. Each type carries a rider on a failed save (cold: –10-foot status penalty to Speeds for 1 round; electricity: off-guard until the end of your next turn; fire: 1d10 persistent-style extra damage, 2d10 on a critical failure, doubling with the wand paragon benefit) — all resolved at the table, not on the sheet.
evidence: "Choose a second damage type from the list; whenever you Fling Magic, you can select between either of the two damage types you have chosen."
engineNote: Three-layer gap. (1) This record is currently UNREACHABLE: nothing in src/ grants adept-benefit-* features, because Implement Adept (see its entry in this chunk) has no implementation — so even a correct choice field here would never be prompted. (2) The PAIRED first pick is missing too: initiate-benefit-wand's "choose whether your wand is attuned to cold, electricity, or fire" has no effectChoices either, so there is nothing for 'a second damage type' to be second to; both records need the field, and the second must exclude the first. (3) The chosen types only matter at roll time (which type this Fling Magic uses, and its rider), so the pick is a recorded, displayed selection with no persistent stat grant — use the grant-less EffectChoice option pattern (options with `note` and no `grant`) that gates-threshold already uses for its play-time junctions. Shape note: this is a classFeature, so the field is `effectChoices` (EffectChoice[]), not the Feat-only `choice`/FeatChoiceDef.
question: The wand implement needs TWO linked damage-type picks (initiate = one of cold/electricity/fire, adept = a different second one) and neither record has a choice field, while the adept records are unreachable until Implement Adept is built. Should the initiate/adept/paragon benefit records be wired into the implement system as part of this pass, or deferred with the wand damage type left unrecorded?

name: Bestiary Scholar
restriction: You must have master proficiency in the chosen skill — the feat's own prerequisite ('master in Arcana, Crafting, Nature, Occultism, or Religion') already gates this.
effect: Record + display only. The chosen skill may Recall Knowledge to identify any creature normally identified by any of the five. The '+1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll or saving throw' only fires after a critical identification, so it is an in-play conditional, not a standing modifier.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose one of the following skills in which you have attained master proficiency: Arcana, Crafting, Nature, Occultism, or Religion."
engineNote: Nothing new required: the pick round-trips through FeatChoice.choice and renders on the feat card. Note FeatChoiceDef has no proficiency filter, so all five options are always offered even to a character who is only expert — acceptable, since the prerequisite blocks the feat anyway.

name: Masterful Obfuscation
openSource: Any skill with the Recall Knowledge action in which you are master — Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or any Lore skill you have.
restriction: master proficiency, and the skill must have a Recall Knowledge use. The feat's prerequisite ('master in a skill with the Recall Knowledge action') restates it.
effect: Display only. When you Lie about facts related to that subject you roll the CHOSEN skill in place of Deception, carrying that skill's bonuses/penalties. No standing modifier changes.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose one skill with the Recall Knowledge action in which you have attained master proficiency."
engineNote: FeatChoiceDef.kind is currently only 'domains' | 'array' — an open skill pool is a new kind. It must include free-text Lore (the text says 'one skill with the Recall Knowledge action', and Lore qualifies), which the existing BuildState.featLoreChoices free-text input already solves for FEAT_GRANTS.loreChoices; the same widget would need to be reachable from a choice. Fallback with zero engine work: kind 'array' over the seven non-Lore RK skills, which silently drops the Lore case.

name: Determined Lore Seeker
restriction: Must be one of the three innate spells the Lore Seeker feat granted (prerequisite: Lore Seeker).
effect: The chosen spell becomes castable 3/day instead of 1/day. Separately (no choice involved, applies to all three): Translate is heightened to rank 4, Sound Body to ceil(level/2), and See the Unseen gains a concentrate action to see invisible creatures normally.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose one of the innate spells granted by the Lore Seeker feat... You can cast this spell three times per day instead of once per day."
engineNote: The pick has to reach back and MUTATE ANOTHER feat's grant: lore-seeker.innateSpells currently reads [translate, sound-body, see-the-unseen] each usesPerDay:1, rank:2. InnateSpellGrant already has usesPerDay / rank / heightenHalfLevel, so every value is expressible — what is missing is a lane for one feat to override another feat's innate grant. DATA DEFECT: this record's description still uses the pre-Remaster names (comprehend language / restore senses / see invisibility) while lore-seeker in core.json already uses the Remaster names; the option values above are the Remaster ids that actually exist in d.spells.

name: Martial Exercise
restriction: None beyond the group list (the 17 weapon groups present in core.json items).
effect: A MIRRORING proficiency grant: whenever any weapon proficiency rank rises to expert or beyond, simple AND martial weapons of the chosen group also gain that rank.
evidence: "Choose one weapon group, such as hammer or sword. Whenever your proficiency rank in any weapon increases to expert or beyond, you also gain that new proficiency rank with both simple and martial weapons of your chosen weapon group."
engineNote: FEAT_GRANTS already has the exact semantics one level down: weaponFamiliarity.mirrorBestCategory ('whenever a class feature grants you expert or greater proficiency in certain weapons, you also gain it for these') — but it is keyed to NAMED weapons. Proficiencies.weaponGroups exists but holds a flat rank, not a mirror. Needs a group-shaped sibling, e.g. weaponGroupFamiliarity: { group: <from choice.value>, categories: ['simple','martial'], mirrorBestCategory: true }, fed by the feat's choice value the way choiceGrants already works.

name: Kreighton's Cognitive Crossover
restriction: Two DIFFERENT skills from the list; the feat's whole function is reattempting with 'the other chosen skill'. No proficiency requirement. Picking 'Lore (any one)' needs a follow-up free-text subject.
effect: Display only — no proficiency or modifier changes. The pair defines the reaction's trigger (a fruitless Recall Knowledge with one of them) and its reroll skill (the other).
evidence: "**Special** When you gain this feat, choose two of the following skills: Arcana, Crafting, Lore (any one), Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, or Society."
engineNote: Feat.choice is singular, so two picks do not fit it. The zero-new-type route is two effectChoices entries (ids 'skill-1'/'skill-2') with options carrying NO grant — EffectChoice explicitly allows grantless options ('An option with no grant simply applies nothing'). Two gaps remain: (a) nothing enforces the two picks being distinct, (b) the 'Lore (any one)' option needs the free-text Lore subject prompt, and it must NOT train that Lore (unlike FEAT_GRANTS.loreChoices, which grants training).

name: Ghost Hunter Dedication
openSource: Two picks: any occult cantrip with the divination, enchantment or necromancy trait. One pick: Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore (a fixed two-option list).
restriction: Each cantrip must carry divination OR enchantment OR necromancy (an OR, not an AND). If already trained in BOTH Spirit Lore and Haunt Lore, the Lore pick converts to any other Lore of your choice.
effect: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED via effectChoices: 'lore' (grant skills lore:spirit / lore:haunt trained) plus 'cantrip-1'/'cantrip-2' (spellFilter traditions:['occult'], cantripsOnly, grantAs innate, atWill).
evidence: "Pick Spirit Lore or Haunt Lore; you become trained in this skill... Choose two cantrips from the occult spell list. Each cantrip must have the divination, enchantment, or necromancy trait."
engineNote: Two residual gaps in the EXISTING data, not missing structure: (1) both cantrip spellFilters omit the trait restriction entirely, so any occult cantrip is offered — SpellChoiceFilter.traits requires ALL listed traits (AND), but this rule is an OR, so it needs an anyTraits/OR field before the filter can be authored; (2) the 'if you were already trained in both' fallback has no expression — FEAT_GRANTS.redundantFallback covers that pattern only for static `skills`, not for an effectChoices option.

name: Spirit Spells
