openSource: Any occult spell of rank 1 (now), rank 2 (at level 6) and rank 3 (at level 8), each with the divination, enchantment or necromancy trait.
restriction: Trait must be divination OR enchantment OR necromancy. Ranks 2 and 3 unlock at character levels 6 and 8.
effect: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED via effectChoices 'occult-1'/'occult-2'/'occult-3' — spellFilter with rank 1/2/3, minLevel 6/8, grantAs innate, innate.usesPerDay 1.
evidence: "Choose a 1st-rank occult spell. You can Cast this Spell as an innate occult spell. At 6th level, you gain a 2nd-rank occult spell, and at 8th level, you gain a 3rd-rank occult spell. Each of these spells must have the divination, enchantment, or necromancy trait."
engineNote: Same single residual gap as Ghost Hunter Dedication: the three spellFilters carry no trait restriction, so the divination/enchantment/necromancy limit is unenforced. SpellChoiceFilter.traits is AND-semantics; an OR (anyTraits) field is the prerequisite for authoring it. Rank gating and the innate 1/day cadence are already correct.

name: Animal Shape
restriction: Locked once taken — the text forbids changing it later, so it is a genuinely permanent build value (unlike most 'choose a form' text).
effect: Change Shape now grants the effects of a 5th-rank casting of the chosen form spell, except you always become your inherent animal and may keep your own AC if higher.
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose either Aerial Form, Animal Form, Dinosaur Form, or Insect Form; after you choose a form, you can't change the form."
engineNote: The pick itself needs no new type. Applying it does: a battle form REPLACES AC, Speeds, senses and Strikes wholesale, and the alternate-form lane (stances with form:true, carrying strike/AC/dexCap/speed/senses) models toggles that layer ON TOP of the character, not a full stat substitution — and the numbers here live in the form spell's prose, not in structured fields. Minimum viable: record the pick and surface the chosen spell's description on the feat card; full battle-form math is a separate subsystem.

name: Eldritch Researcher Dedication
openSource: Pick 1: any arcane OR occult cantrip. Pick 2 (independent): Arcana or Occultism, a fixed two-option list.
restriction: The cantrip's tradition determines which tradition you become trained in; the skill pick is explicitly independent of it ('Regardless of whether you choose an arcane or occult cantrip').
effect: Cantrip: cast as an innate spell heightened to ceil(level/2), and you become trained in that tradition's spell DC/attack with Intelligence. Skill: expert in the picked skill, plus a +1 circumstance bonus with it when Investigating or Identifying Magic.
evidence: "You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or occult cantrip of your choice (which is heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up)... you also become an expert in your choice of either Arcana or Occultism."
engineNote: The Foundry record backs this exactly: a ChoiceSet flagged 'eldritch' over Arcana/Occultism + ActiveEffectLike upgrading that skill's rank to 2 + a predicated FlatModifier +1 (action:investigate / action:identify-magic). The SKILL half needs no engine work — FEAT_GRANTS.skillChoices: [{ options: ['arcana','occultism'], rank: 'expert' }] is an existing lane. The CANTRIP half needs an effectChoices spellFilter { traditions: ['arcane','occult'], cantripsOnly: true, grantAs: 'innate', innate: { heightenHalfLevel: true } }. What is genuinely missing: SpellcastingGrant is a static single-tradition field, so 'trained in THAT tradition's spell DCs, Int key' cannot follow the chosen cantrip's tradition, and the innate grant's tradition must likewise be derived from the pick. The +1 circumstance bonus is action-predicated and stays prose-only.

name: Standby Spell
openSource: Spells in YOUR OWN magus spellbook (BuildState.spellbook), not the whole arcane list.
restriction: Rank no higher than your highest magus slot, and it must be a spell usable with Spellstrike. Re-selectable, but only when you add spells to your spellbook or study it for an hour — so it is a persistent, editable build value, not a per-use pick.
effect: You can cast the chosen spell without preparing it, by expending a slot of sufficient rank.
evidence: "Choose a spell in your spellbook that you could use with Spellstrike and that has a level no higher than the highest-level magus spell slot you have."
engineNote: Three gaps. (1) SpellChoiceFilter draws from a TRADITION, not from the character's own spellbook — a 'from your spellbook' source is new (BuildState.spellbook: Record<number,string[]> already exists to read from). (2) There is no Spellstrike-eligibility flag on Spell (Spellstrike needs a spell with a spell attack roll or one that targets a single creature), so the filter cannot be expressed. (3) grantAs is 'innate' | 'focus' only; this is a third mode — cast unprepared by spending a slot.

name: Arcane Shroud
restriction: Exactly three, all distinct, from the seven listed. All seven ids verified present in core.json spells.
effect: Display only at build time — the three picks form the menu you choose from in play when you Arcane Cascade (the fourth, at-use pick is NOT a build choice). No standing modifier.
evidence: "When you take this feat, choose three of False Vitality, Fire Shield, Fleet Step, Flicker, , Mountain Resilience, and See the Unseen."
engineNote: DATA DEFECT FIRST: the double comma in the quoted text is a dropped spell — the Foundry source (.import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/feats/class/magus/level-14/arcane-shroud.json) lists SEVEN, and the missing one is INVISIBILITY. descRefs is likewise short by one. Fix the description before authoring the choice. Then: Feat.choice is singular, so three picks need three effectChoices entries with grantless options; nothing enforces distinctness, which matters more here than for Kreighton's because duplicates would silently shrink the menu.

name: Advanced Weaponry
restriction: Two picks: first WHICH starting melee unarmed attack (EidolonConfig has exactly two — primary and secondary), then which trait it gains. Both are permanent (evolution trait).
effect: The chosen eidolon unarmed attack permanently gains the chosen trait.
evidence: "Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks. It gains one of the following traits, chosen when you gain the feat: disarm, grapple, nonlethal, shove, trip, or versatile bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing."
engineNote: EidolonConfig.primary/secondary are { name?, damageType?, option? } only — there is no per-attack extra-traits lane. In deriveEidolon the primary's traits come from EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS[option].traits and the secondary's are hardcoded ['agile','finesse'], so a feat cannot add one. Needs an extraTraits?: string[] on each attack, fed by this feat's picks. NOTE this feat is also the ONLY route to a grapple-traited eidolon attack — EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS has no grapple entry — which makes it a hard prerequisite for Grasping Limbs in this data set.

name: Dual Studies
openSource: Any two skills — the text places no restriction at all. One is assigned to you, the other to your eidolon.
restriction: Two distinct skills; you must also say which one goes to the eidolon. Both rise to expert at character level 7, and the two proficiencies are explicitly NOT shared.
effect: You: trained in your skill, expert at 7. Eidolon: trained in its skill, expert at 7.
evidence: "Choose two skills. Your eidolon becomes trained in one of those skills and you become trained in the other skill. At 7th level, you each become an expert in the chosen skills. These skill proficiencies are not shared between you and your eidolon."
engineNote: The CHARACTER half needs no engine work: FEAT_GRANTS entry with skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] plus rankUpgrade: { level: 7, rank: 'expert' } — both existing lanes, and rankUpgrade already applies to choice-driven grants. The EIDOLON half has no lane: the eidolon block's skills come from the summoner subclass option's grants.skills (a flat string list) and the eidolon has no skill-proficiency model at all, so 'trained now, expert at 7' cannot be represented. Needs eidolon skill proficiencies before the second pick means anything.

name: Energy Heart
restriction: Any energy damage type EXCEPT force — i.e. the eight energy types minus force. The list matches Eidolon's Wrath's explicit enumeration in the same book, which is the confirming cross-reference.
effect: One of the eidolon's unarmed attacks changes its damage type to the chosen type, and the eidolon gains resistance to that type equal to max(1, floor(level / 2)). Permanent (evolution trait).
evidence: "Choose an energy damage type other than force. One of its unarmed attacks changes its damage type to the chosen type, and it gains resistance to that type equal to half your level (minimum 1)."
engineNote: Small and pattern-matched: deriveEidolon in src/rules/companions.ts already does exactly this for the follow-up feat — `if (featIdSet.has('dual-energy-heart')) { const chosen = ...?.choice?.value; evoIwr.push(`resistance ${Math.max(1, Math.floor(level / 2))} ${chosen}`) }` — but there is NO branch for energy-heart itself, so the base feat contributes nothing. Add the mirror branch. The damage-type half needs no work: the player already sets EidolonConfig.primary/secondary.damageType by hand, though the feat does not say WHICH attack, so consider a second pick (primary/secondary) rather than leaving it implicit.

name: Dual Energy Heart
restriction: An ADDITIONAL energy type, so it should exclude the one already picked for Energy Heart (prerequisite). Force is excluded, inheriting Energy Heart's restriction.
effect: The eidolon's energy-damage unarmed attack gains versatile for the second type, and the eidolon gains resistance to it equal to floor(level / 2).
evidence: "Choose an additional energy damage type. Your eidolon's unarmed attack that deals energy damage gains the versatile trait for the second energy damage type, and your eidolon gains resistance to the second type of energy damage equal to half your level."
engineNote: HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM IN THIS CHUNK — the engine is already waiting for this field. src/rules/companions.ts reads it verbatim: `const chosen = character.feats.find((f) => f.featId === 'dual-energy-heart')?.choice?.value;` and then pushes `resistance N ${chosen ?? 'chosen energy type'}` into the eidolon's IWR line. Because the record has no `choice`, every summoner's eidolon block currently prints the literal placeholder 'resistance N chosen energy type'. Adding the choice above fixes it end to end with zero code changes. The versatile-trait half still has no lane (same gap as Advanced Weaponry) and is already covered by the existing evoNotes reminder.

name: Eidolon's Wrath
restriction: The seven types are enumerated outright. A conditional extra option exists for celestial/fiend/monitor eidolons of non-neutral alignment.
effect: Sets the damage type of the Eidolon's Wrath focus spell (5d6, +2d6 per heighten, basic Reflex) that this feat already grants via focusSpells.
evidence: "You determine the damage type when you gain the feat: acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, vitality, or void."
engineNote: The granted spell (d.spells['eidolons-wrath']) has baseDamage '5d6' but its type is prose — 'damage of the type you chose when you took the Eidolon's Wrath feat'. There is no per-character damage-type override for a granted focus spell, so even with the pick stored the spell card still reads 'the type you chose'. Minimum viable: record it and show it on the feat/spell card; proper fix is a damage-type override on the focus-spell grant.
question: The feat's second clause ('If your eidolon is a celestial, fiend, or monitor with an alignment other than true neutral, you can choose a damage type in its alignment') is pre-Remaster alignment damage. This project already remapped alignment damage to SPIRIT elsewhere. Should the option list gain a conditional 'spirit' entry, keep legacy good/evil/lawful/chaotic, or drop the clause entirely?

name: Magical Adept
openSource: One rank-2 spell and one rank-1 spell of YOUR EIDOLON'S tradition — the tradition is derived from the chosen eidolon type (the subclass option's `tradition`), so the pool is per-character, not a fixed list.
restriction: Exactly one at rank 2 and one at rank 1; both must be of the eidolon's tradition. From every even level onward one may be swapped for another at least 2 ranks below your highest slot (retraining, out of scope).
effect: The EIDOLON — not the summoner — can cast each once per day as an innate spell.
evidence: "Choose one 2nd-rank spell and one 1st-rank spell of your eidolon's tradition. Your eidolon can cast them each once per day as innate spells."
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) The grant lands on the COMPANION: InnateSpellGrant/effectChoices route spells onto the character's innate entry, and CompanionConfig has no spell lane at all, so an eidolon innate-spell list is new. (2) SpellChoiceFilter.traditions is a static array, but here the tradition must be resolved from the chosen eidolon type at build time — a dynamic-tradition filter is new too. Rank 1/rank 2 and usesPerDay 1 are already expressible.

name: Pushing Attack
restriction: The chosen attack must have the SHOVE trait. In this data set only the primary can: EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS includes 'd8-shove', while the secondary is hardcoded agile + finesse. So unless Advanced Weaponry added shove to the secondary, the pick is forced and the prompt is near-degenerate.
effect: That eidolon unarmed attack gains the Push action.
evidence: "Choose one of the eidolon's unarmed attacks with the shove trait. It gains the Push action for that attack."
engineNote: Nothing renders a per-attack granted action on a companion Strike, and the options cannot be validated against the shove trait at build time (primary traits are resolved in deriveEidolon from EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS, not stored on the build). Needs the same per-attack rider lane as Advanced Weaponry/Weighty Impact/Grasping Limbs — one shared field (e.g. grantedActions on the eidolon attack) covers all four feats.

name: Weighty Impact
restriction: The chosen attack must have the TRIP trait. As with Pushing Attack, only the primary can in this data set ('d8-trip' in EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS); the secondary is fixed at agile + finesse.
effect: That eidolon unarmed attack gains the Knockdown action.
evidence: "Choose one of the eidolon's unarmed attacks with the trip trait. It gains the Knockdown action for that attack."
engineNote: Identical to Pushing Attack: no per-attack granted-action lane on companion Strikes, and the trip-trait restriction cannot be enforced on the picker. Solve once for all four eidolon-attack-rider feats.

name: Grasping Limbs
restriction: The chosen attack must have the GRAPPLE trait — and in this data set NO eidolon attack can have it natively: EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS offers only disarm / nonlethal / shove / trip / fatal / forceful+sweep / deadly+finesse, and the secondary is fixed at agile + finesse. Grapple is reachable only via the Advanced Weaponry feat, which lists it explicitly.
effect: That eidolon unarmed attack gains the Grab action.
evidence: "Choose one of the eidolon's unarmed attacks with the grapple trait. It gains the Grab action on that unarmed attack."
engineNote: Same missing per-attack rider lane as Pushing Attack / Weighty Impact, plus a prerequisite gap worth checking: because EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS has no grapple entry, this feat is currently unsatisfiable unless Advanced Weaponry granted grapple. Either the primary-attack option table is missing a grapple variant from Secrets of Magic, or Grasping Limbs genuinely depends on Advanced Weaponry — worth verifying against the printed eidolon attack table before wiring the picker.
question: Should EIDOLON_PRIMARY_OPTIONS include a '1d8 (grapple)' entry? The app's table lists disarm/nonlethal/shove/trip only, which leaves Grasping Limbs unreachable without Advanced Weaponry — is that the printed rule or a missing option?

name: Dracomancer
openSource: Two picks, already present as effectChoices with spellFilter {rank:1} and {rank:2}, grantAs 'innate', usesPerDay 1. The correct pool is the spell list of a dragon spellcaster of the character's draconic benefactor type — that list does not exist in core.json (draconicExemplar records are name-only stubs), so the shipped filter is an unrestricted any-tradition rank-1/rank-2 spell search.
restriction: "from those listed for a dragon spellcaster of your draconic benefactor's type" — and the tradition must be "the same tradition as your draconic benefactor", not the hardcoded arcane in this record's spellcastingGrant.
effect: Each picked spell becomes an innate spell castable once per day; trained spell attack/DC, key attribute Charisma.
evidence: "Choose one 1st-rank spell and one 2nd-rank spell from those listed for a dragon spellcaster of your draconic benefactor's type … You can cast each of these spells once per day as innate spells of the same tradition as your draconic benefactor."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) There is no 'draconic benefactor' choice anywhere in the build — grep of core.json finds no feat/heritage that records one, and the prerequisite heritage dragonscaled-kobold carries no benefactor field. Without it the tradition cannot be derived, so spellcastingGrant.tradition is frozen at 'arcane'. A reusable option table already exists: classes.sorcerer.subclass.options['bloodline-draconic'].dragonChoice (44 exemplars, each with tradition/skill/damageType). (2) Dragon-spellcaster spell lists are not in the data, so SpellChoiceFilter cannot express the real restriction.
question: Should a character-level 'draconic benefactor' pick be added (reusing the sorcerer dragonChoice table) so Dracomancer's tradition and spell pool follow it — or is the current unrestricted any-tradition rank-1/rank-2 picker acceptable, with a dataWarning noting the dragon spell lists are missing?

name: Elite Dracomancer
openSource: Two picks, already present as effectChoices with spellFilter {rank:3} and {rank:4}, grantAs 'innate', usesPerDay 1. Same missing pool as Dracomancer — dragon-spellcaster lists are absent from core.json, so the filter is an unrestricted any-tradition rank-3/rank-4 search.
restriction: "from those listed for a dragon spellcaster of your draconic benefactor's type"; tradition follows the benefactor (this record inherits Dracomancer's spellcasting profile).
effect: Each picked spell becomes an innate spell castable once per day.
evidence: "Choose one 3rd-rank spell and one 4th-rank spell from those listed for a dragon spellcaster of your draconic benefactor's type … You can cast each of these spells once per day as innate spells of the same tradition as your draconic benefactor."
engineNote: Identical to Dracomancer: needs the draconic-benefactor pick to exist and dragon-spellcaster spell lists in the data. Prerequisite chain means it should also inherit the benefactor choice rather than re-prompt.
question: Same benefactor question as Dracomancer — add a benefactor pick that both feats read, or keep the unrestricted rank-3/rank-4 picker with a dataWarning?

name: Draconic Acolyte Dedication
openSource: The draconic-exemplar table already in the data: classes.sorcerer.subclass.options['bloodline-draconic'].dragonChoice (44 entries, each with a tradition), filtered to the tradition that matches the skill used to qualify.
restriction: "a trait that matches the trained skill you used to qualify for this feat (arcane for Arcana, primal for Nature, occult for Occultism, and divine for Religion)" — and it is permanent: "You can't change your draconic benefactor later."
effect: Sets the tradition trait carried by the draconic gift item and by Channel Draconic Essence, Draconic Salvation, and every other feat in this archetype. Two secondary picks ride along: the gift item's appearance (pure flavor, no mechanics) and — only if already trained in Dragon Lore — a free Lore skill.
evidence: "Choose a [dragon] with a trait that matches the trained skill you used to qualify for this feat (arcane for Arcana, primal for Nature, occult for Occultism, and divine for Religion). You can't change your draconic benefactor later."
engineNote: Feat.choice can STORE and display the benefactor, but nothing consumes it: there is no lane that stamps a tradition trait onto an archetype's granted actions. Separately, the second clause — "You gain the Additional Lore feat for Dragon Lore. If you were already trained in Dragon Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice" — is a CONDITIONAL loreChoice: FEAT_GRANTS currently holds only `{ skills: { 'lore:dragon': 'trained' } }` (featGrantsAuto.ts), and `redundantFallback` converts a redundant grant to a free SKILL pick, not to a free LORE pick. A conditional loreChoices lane (or extending redundantFallback to lore targets) is needed.

name: Expert Skysage Divination
restriction: Three SEPARATE level-gated one-of-two picks, not one pick of six: 4th-rank pair at level 10, 5th-rank pair at level 12, 6th-rank pair at level 14. EffectChoice.spellFilter.minLevel already expresses the gating; as an options-list this needs three EffectChoice entries.
effect: Each pick is added to the character's Oatia skysage spell repertoire (a spontaneous occult archetype repertoire). The feat also raises occult spell attack/DC to expert — a proficiency step, not a choice.
evidence: "You choose one of the following 4th-rank spells to add to your spell repertoire: or Read Omens. At 12th level, choose one of the following 5th-rank spells … Mind Probe or Scouting Eye. At 14th level, choose one of the following 6th-rank spells … Scrying or Truesight."
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) No repertoire-grant lane: EffectGrant supports only innateSpells and focusSpells, and SpellChoiceFilter.grantAs is 'innate' | 'focus'. The existing Oatia precedent (oatia-skysage-dedication) smuggles its two CANTRIPS in as innateSpells with atWill:true, which is a fair approximation for cantrips but would be wrong for a 4th–6th-rank repertoire spell (it would read as 1/day innate instead of castable from archetype slots). Needs either grantAs:'repertoire' feeding SpellcastingEntry.grantedRepertoire, or an EffectGrant.repertoireSpells lane. (2) oatia-skysage-dedication is NOT in CASTER_ARCHETYPES (casterArchetypes.ts), so the archetype has no spell slots at all — the repertoire additions have nothing to be cast from. A CasterArchetype entry with customUnlocks + profExpertFeat/profMasterFeat (the Halcyon Speaker pattern) is the matching fix.
question: The record's own text has a dropped spell name — "one of the following 4th-rank spells … : or Read Omens" (the same AoN unsubstituted-template defect; the sibling Basic Skysage Divination shows it too, "…3rd-rank spells: or Locate"). The missing option is almost certainly Clairvoyance (rank 4, arcane/occult, present in core.json and the only other 4th-rank Oatia divination). Confirm Clairvoyance before it is written into the options list?

name: Master Skysage Divination
restriction: Only the 7th-rank entry is a choice. The 18th- and 20th-level additions are AUTOMATIC and must not be prompted: "At 18th level, add Pinpoint to your spell repertoire, and at 20th level, add Foresight to your spell repertoire."
effect: The pick (at level 16) plus the automatic Pinpoint (18) and Foresight (20) enter the Oatia skysage repertoire. The feat also raises occult spell attack/DC to master.
evidence: "You choose one of the following 7th-rank spells to add to your spell repertoire: or True Target. At 18th level, add Pinpoint to your spell repertoire, and at 20th level, add Foresight to your spell repertoire."
engineNote: Same repertoire-grant and missing-CasterArchetype blockers as Expert Skysage Divination. Note the two automatic grants (Pinpoint L18, Foresight L20) are a level-gated fixed grant, which also has no lane on a feat — Feat.focusSpells is focus-only and innateSpells carries no level gate for a repertoire add.
question: Same dropped-name defect: "one of the following 7th-rank spells: or True Target". The missing option is almost certainly Retrocognition (rank 7, arcane/occult, present in core.json). Confirm before writing it into the options list?

name: Avenging Runelord Dedication
restriction: Permanent; one of exactly these five (pride and lust are absent from the list).
effect: The sin defines an alternative pool for this feat's innate spell ("any spell of 6th rank or lower from the sin spells listed for your chosen sin") and is read by two later archetype feats — expanded-runelord-magic (L14) and advanced-runelord-magic (L18) both say "magic associated with your chosen sin".
evidence: "Choose one of the following sins: envy, gluttony, greed, sloth, or wrath."
engineNote: The sin pick itself fits Feat.choice kind 'array' as-is. What it CANNOT drive: the sin spell lists are not in core.json (no 'sin' collection exists), so the innate-spell effectChoice already on this record enumerates only the seven named spells and silently drops the "alternatively … any spell of 6th rank or lower from the sin spells listed for your chosen sin" branch. Three further NON-choice gaps on the same record are also unmodeled and worth the same pass: (a) "You become trained in Arcana. If you are already trained in Arcana, you become trained in the skill of your choice" plus expert at 14 and master at 16 — a FEAT_GRANTS entry with skills+redundantFallback+rankUpgrade, currently absent from both featGrants.ts and featGrantsAuto.ts; (b) "You have familiarity with weapons in the polearm and spear weapon groups — … treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons" — FEAT_GRANTS.weaponFamiliarity takes named weapon BASES with a flat rank, so a GROUP-scoped category downshift has no lane; (c) "You learn the Thassilonian language" — a plain grantsLanguages:['thassilonian'] backfill (the language id exists in core.json).
question: The sin spell lists (the Thassilonian sin-magic school lists) are not in the shipped data. Should the sin-spell branch of the innate-spell pick be left out with a dataWarning, or do you want the five lists sourced and added so the choice can offer them?

name: Heroic Scion Dedication
restriction: Any skill that is not a Lore skill. The text adds "Your GM can help you determine a list of appropriate skills to choose from", so the pool is all non-Lore skills with GM curation — do not try to enumerate a themed subset.
effect: Unlocks an opt-in ability: when using that skill you may spend a Mythic Point to attempt the check at mythic proficiency. It does NOT raise the skill's normal rank, so it must not be applied as a proficiency grant.
evidence: "Choose one skill that's not a Lore skill, based on the themes of your reincarnated heroic source. … When you employ an action using that skill, you may spend a Mythic Point to attempt the associated check at mythic proficiency."
engineNote: Storing the pick is easy (Feat.choice with a skills kind). Applying it is not: the engine has no 'alternate proficiency you may opt into by spending a resource' lane — FEAT_GRANTS.skills/skillChoices only ever RAISE a permanent rank, which would be flatly wrong here. Minimum honest behaviour: record and display the skill and surface the mythic-proficiency option as a note on that skill. Non-choice items on the same record that are also unmodeled: the Additional Lore grant for the fixed subject 'Incarnation Lore', the recovery-check DC −1, and the +2 circumstance bonus to Perception vs the nemesis (conditional, leave in prose). The nemesis itself is GM-determined narrative and needs no prompt.

name: Psychic Dedication
restriction: A SECOND, dependent pick follows it: one standard psi cantrip drawn only from the conscious mind just chosen. The standard psi cantrips per mind are already in core.json at classes.psychic.subclass.options[<mind>].grantedSpells, entries 10 and 11 — Distant Grasp: telekinetic-hand / telekinetic-projectile; Infinite Eye: detect-magic / guidance; Oscillating Wave: frostbite / ignition; Silent Whisper: daze / message; Tangible Dream: figment / shield; Unbound Step: phase-bolt / warp-step.
effect: Grants the archetype's one repertoire cantrip, cast as a psi cantrip (so it can be amped) with the conscious mind's passive rider — but explicitly nothing else from that mind: "You gain the normal benefits for this psi cantrip, but not any other benefits from the conscious mind."
evidence: "Choose a conscious mind. You gain a spell repertoire with one standard psi cantrip of your choice from your conscious mind, which you cast as a psi cantrip."
engineNote: psychic-dedication IS already wired into CASTER_ARCHETYPES (casterArchetypes.ts: occult, choiceKeyAbility ['int','cha'], cantrips: 1) — but that gives ONE unrestricted occult cantrip and never asks for a conscious mind, so the mind is lost and the cantrip pool is wrong. Two engine gaps: (1) DEPENDENT choices — EffectChoice.options is a static list, so choice B's options cannot be a function of choice A's value; (2) the cantrip must be a psi cantrip (ampable), and there is no lane marking an archetype-granted cantrip as psi. The skill half ("trained in Occultism; if you were already trained in Occultism, you become trained in a skill of your choice") is already correct in featGrantsAuto.ts: `{ skills: { occultism: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }`.
question: Confirm the two standard psi cantrips for The Unbound Step. I read them positionally out of classes.psychic.subclass.options — phase-bolt and warp-step — and the other five minds' pairs check out against the printed lists, but I could not verify Unbound Step's independently.

name: Thaumaturge Dedication
restriction: All ten implements are legal; the ids above are exactly the keys of core.json's top-level `implement` collection (also enumerated as classes.thaumaturge.extraChoices['implement'].options).
effect: Record-only. "you can use it to Glimpse Vulnerability, but don't gain its benefits" — the pick grants NO initiate/adept/paragon benefit, so it must be stored and displayed but must not be wired to any implement effect. Storing it matters because Glimpse Vulnerability requires "You are holding your implement".
evidence: "Choose an implement; you can use it to Glimpse Vulnerability, but don't gain its benefits."
engineNote: Feat.choice kind 'array' covers this as-is (display-only, like the 110 existing array choices). SEPARATE BUG on the same record: the second sentence is "You become trained in your choice of Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion; if you were already trained in these, you become trained in a skill of your choice", but featGrantsAuto.ts currently holds `'thaumaturge-dedication': { skillChoices: [{ options: 'any', rank: 'trained' }] }` — an unrestricted any-skill pick. It should be `skillChoices: [{ options: ['arcana','nature','occultism','religion'], rank: 'trained' }]` with the already-trained fallback, which today lets a player train any skill they like off this dedication.

name: Echo of the Fallen
openSource: Two picks: (1) any MARTIAL weapon — or any ADVANCED weapon if the character is trained in all martial weapons — drawn from core.json items filtered to weapons of that category; (2) any skill (no Lore restriction stated).
restriction: Permanent: "once you've chosen the weapon and skill, you can't change them." The advanced-weapon option unlocks only if the character is trained in all martial weapons. The text also says "work with your GM", so treat both pools as open with GM curation rather than a themed subset.
effect: Nothing while dormant. While the granted Accept Echo action is active (10 minutes, once per day) the character becomes trained in the chosen weapon and expert in the chosen skill, scaling to master in the skill at 7th, expert in the weapon at 13th, and legendary in the skill at 15th.
evidence: "work with your GM to choose one martial weapon and one skill (or an advanced weapon if you're trained in all martial weapons) that are appropriate for the spirit; once you've chosen the weapon and skill, you can't change them."
engineNote: The picks are storable, but the effect is not expressible. DefenseGrants.whileActive is limited to the four signature states 'rage' | 'panache' | 'hunt-prey' | 'unleash-psyche' and its payload covers only resistances/senses/immunities/speeds — no skill or weapon proficiency, and no way to declare a NEW toggle state ('echo'). Applying the proficiencies unconditionally via FEAT_GRANTS would be wrong (they only exist for 10 minutes a day). Needs either a custom toggle state with proficiency payloads, or the picks recorded plus a prose note.

name: Split Slot
chooses: other (a spell RANK, plus a second prepared spell to put in that rank's slot)
restriction: The rank must be at least 1 lower than the highest-rank spell you can cast (so the picker must be clamped by character level).
effect: That rank gets one EXTRA prepared spell; only one of the two paired spells can actually be cast that day (the other dissipates).
evidence: "you can choose one spell slot at least 1 rank lower than the highest-rank spell you can cast and prepare two spells in that slot. When you Cast a Spell from that slot, choose which spell to cast."
engineNote: Heroes Heaven models daily preparation in the builder (BuildState.spells is the prepared list), so the rank pick IS build-time here. There is no lane for it: Feat.spellSlotBonus only does {perRank, exceptHighest, entryId} — a flat per-rank bonus — not 'one extra prepared spell at ONE chosen rank, of which only one may be cast'. Feat.choice can record the rank (display-only) but cannot add the slot.
question: Should Split Slot add a real extra prepared-spell slot at the chosen rank (which overstates power, since only one of the two paired spells can be cast), or should it only record the rank + show a note on the Spells page?

name: Bard Dedication
chooses: other (a bard muse — the class's subclass option)
restriction: None — any bard muse; you gain none of its starting feat/spell/abilities.
effect: Records the muse and qualifies you for that muse's bard feats (e.g. Bardic Lore requires "enigma muse"). No stat effect of its own.
evidence: "Choose a muse as you would if you were a bard. You can take that muse's feats, but you don't gain the starting feat, spell or any other abilities the choice of muse grants."
engineNote: Options come straight from content.classes.bard.subclass.options (5 muses). Feat.choice is display-only in this engine (only kind 'domains' feeds a grant, via the focus lane) — which is fine here because muse feat prerequisites are unenforced free text in featSlots.ts, so the pick needs no gating work. SEPARATE DATA BUG spotted in the same record: the skill clause is "You become trained in Occultism and Performance; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice", but FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['bard-dedication'] is { skills: { occultism:'trained', performance:'trained' } } with NO redundantFallback:true, so a bard-trained character silently loses the replacement picks.

name: Cleric Dedication
openSource: content.deities (485 records) — the same picker the cleric class already uses (BuildState.deityId)
restriction: Any deity you could choose as a cleric.
effect: Sets the character's deity: you become trained in that deity's associated skill (deity.skill), bound by its anathema, and may receive its sanctification. You gain no other deity abilities (no favored-weapon training, no font).
evidence: "Choose a deity as you would if you were a cleric. You become bound by that deity's anathema and can receive that deity's divine sanctification. You become trained in Religion and your deity's associated skill"
engineNote: The deity picker exists but is class-gated: buildNeedsDeity() (src/rules/build.ts:756) returns true only when the CLASS chooses a deity or the picked subclass has requiresDeity — a fighter taking Cleric Dedication never sees it. Extending that predicate with a 'deity-choosing dedication feat is taken' clause is the small engine change; deity.skill then supplies the second trained skill. Current data is wrong meanwhile: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['cleric-dedication'] = { skills:{religion:'trained'}, skillChoices:[{options:'any',rank:'trained'}] } gives a FREE any-skill instead of the deity's skill, and has no redundantFallback for an already-trained Religion.

name: Druid Dedication
chooses: other (a druidic order — the class's subclass option)
restriction: Any druidic order; you gain none of its other abilities (no order spell, no order feat).
effect: You join that order: trained in its associated skill, bound by its anathema, and qualified for its order feats (e.g. Fire Lung requires "flame order").
evidence: "Choose a druidic order. You become a member of that order and are also bound by its specific anathema, allowing you to take the order's feats. You become trained in Nature and your order's associated skill"
engineNote: Each order option already carries grants.skills (animal-order → athletics, wave-order → …), so the cleanest expression is an effectChoices entry whose 9 options each carry grant:{skills:{<order skill>:'trained'}} — that lane already applies skills (buildCharacter's applyAlwaysOn). Feat.choice alone would only record the label. Current data is wrong: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['druid-dedication'] = { skills:{nature:'trained'}, skillChoices:[{options:'any',rank:'trained'}] } hands out a FREE any-skill instead of the order's skill. The Wildsong language is automatic (no choice).

name: Witch Dedication
chooses: other (a witch patron — the class's subclass option)
restriction: Any witch patron; you gain nothing from it except its tradition.
effect: The patron sets the archetype's spell tradition (patron.tradition) — which in turn sets the familiar's 2 cantrips and the ONE skill you become trained in (the tradition's skill: Arcana/Nature/Occultism/Religion).
evidence: "Choose a Patron; you gain a familiar with two common cantrips of your choice from your chosen patron's tradition, but aside from the tradition, you don't gain any other effects the patron would usually grant." … "You become trained in the skill associated with the patron's tradition; if you were already trained in it, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice."
engineNote: Today CASTER_ARCHETYPES marks witch-dedication choiceTradition:true, so the builder asks for a raw TRADITION (BuildState.archetypeTradition) instead of a patron — a legal shortcut, but it loses the patron record and mis-grants the skill: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['witch-dedication'] = { skillChoices:[{options:'any',rank:'trained'}] } gives a FREE any-skill, when RAW it must be the tradition's skill (only free if you were already trained). Every patron option already carries both `tradition` and `grants.skills`, so a patron pick could drive both.
question: Replace the Witch Dedication tradition picker with a patron picker (patron.tradition then feeds archetypeTradition and patron.grants.skills feeds the skill), or keep the tradition picker and just fix the skill grant to be tradition-derived?

name: Wizard Dedication
chooses: other (an arcane school — the class's subclass option)
restriction: Any wizard school; explicitly grants none of its abilities.
effect: Record-only: you count as a member of that school, which qualifies you for its feats (e.g. Advanced School Spell requires "arcane school").
evidence: "Select a school; you don't gain any abilities from your choice of school, but qualify for feats as a member."
engineNote: Options = content.classes.wizard.subclass.options (14). Nothing mechanical to apply — Feat.choice (display-only) is exactly the right lane. Note the runelord/red-mantis entries are class-archetype schools; the owner may want to trim them from this list. The 4 cantrips + Arcana training are already handled (CASTER_ARCHETYPES + FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS with redundantFallback).

name: Additional Lore
openSource: free-text Lore subject (BuildState.featLoreChoices, granted as lore:<subject>)
restriction: A new Lore subcategory each time the feat is taken (maxTakable = null, unlimited).
effect: Trained in that Lore, plus extra skill increases at levels 3, 7 and 15 that may ONLY be spent on that Lore.
evidence: "Choose a Lore skill subcategory. You become trained in it. At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory."
engineNote: ALREADY WIRED for the training half: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['additional-lore'] = { loreChoices: 1 } and the builder types the subject into BuildState.featLoreChoices — no `choice` field needed. NOT modelled: the three bonus, Lore-restricted skill increases at 3/7/15 (FeatGrant has rankUpgrade for a flat rank bump, but nothing that adds restricted skill-increase slots). Auto-scaling the chosen Lore to expert@3 / master@7 / legendary@15 via rankUpgrade would be a close approximation.

name: Adopted Ancestry
openSource: content.ancestries (50 records; common rarity, or any you have access to) — exclude your own ancestry
restriction: Common ancestries (or ones you have access to); the GM may still veto adopted feats that need a physiological feature you lack.
effect: Ancestry feats of the chosen ancestry become legal picks in your ancestry feat slots, in addition to your own ancestry's.
evidence: "Choose a common ancestry or another ancestry to which you have access. You can select ancestry feats from the ancestry you chose, in addition to your character's own ancestry"
engineNote: The pick can be recorded today, but it does nothing: eligibleFeatsForSlot (src/rules/featSlots.ts:55) hard-gates ancestry slots with `if (p.category === 'ancestry' && build.ancestryId && !f.traits.includes(build.ancestryId)) return false;`. Engine change = also accept the adopted ancestry's trait. Also needed: an 'ancestries' option source (Feat.choice today resolves only 'domains' dynamically, everything else from a literal options array) — enumerating 50 ancestries inline would work but is ugly.

name: Pet
chooses: other (two pet abilities; plus the optional aquatic variant and the animal's flavour type)
restriction: Exactly two; an animal that naturally has one of these (an owl has fly) must take that one.
effect: The pet companion gains the two chosen abilities (senses/speeds/HP).
evidence: "**Pet Abilities** When you gain your pet, choose two of the following abilities." (Amphibious, Burrower, Climber, Darkvision, Echolocation, Fast Movement, Flier, Manual Dexterity, Scent, Tough)
engineNote: ALREADY COVERED — no `choice` field needed: COMPANION_GRANTS['pet'] = { kind:'familiar', abilityBudget:2 } routes it through the existing familiar-ability picker, and all ten pet abilities exist as ids in content.familiarAbilities. Two small gaps if you want it exact: (1) the picker offers the FULL familiar-ability list, so a pet can currently take Speech, Spellcasting, Valet, etc. — a per-grant allow-list would restrict it to the ten above; (2) the "aquatic pet" variant (swim Speed instead of land Speed, aquatic trait) has no toggle.

name: Sequestered Spell
openSource: any cantrip from the spell list of your magiphage ability (arcane / divine / occult / primal)
restriction: Must come from your magiphage ability's tradition.
effect: You cast that cantrip at will as an innate spell, heightened to half your level rounded up.
evidence: "Choose one cantrip from the spell list of your magiphage ability. You can cast this cantrip as an innate spell at will."
engineNote: ALREADY AUTHORED — the record carries effectChoices[0] with spellFilter { cantripsOnly:true, grantAs:'innate', innate:{ atWill:true, heightenHalfLevel:true } }, which the open-spell picker handles. The one defect: the filter has NO `traditions` restriction, because the surki 'magiphage' ability does not exist anywhere in core.json — the surki ancestry record has no such feature, and four other feats (surki-lore, consume-magic, magitaxis, actions/dampening-harmonics) reference it as an unresolvable dangling concept. So the player is currently offered every cantrip in the game.
question: The surki 'magiphage' ability (which fixes a tradition and is referenced by 5 surki records) is missing from core.json. Should we add it as an ancestry-level tradition choice (arcane/divine/occult/primal) so Sequestered Spell's cantrip list and Consume Magic / Magitaxis triggers can be filtered by it?

name: Secondary Adaptation
restriction: Must be a surki heritage you don't already have — filter out BuildState.heritageId (and any heritage gained from a previous take of this feat).
effect: You gain that heritage and all of its benefits (e.g. Breaker's claw Strike, Hardshell's carapace armor, Elytron's no-fall-damage, Lantern's light).
evidence: "Choose one surki heritage that you don't already have; you gain that heritage and its benefits."
engineNote: Heritage is a single build slot (BuildState.heritageId) and nothing applies a SECOND heritage's grants. The heritage records do carry the right structured lanes already (breaker-surki has grantedStrikes; hardshell's carapace is prose-only armor), so the engine work is a 'bonus heritage' lane that merges a second heritage record's DefenseGrants/grantedStrikes — plus dynamic option filtering (exclude the one you have), which Feat.choice's static options array cannot do today.

name: Grand Metamorphosis
chooses: other (one Evolution of a surki heritage you have)

options.label: Breaker — Digging Wedge (claw becomes 1d6, magical/razing/versatile force)

engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and the rank handling is right — maxRank: 3 admits lower-rank spells and innate.rank: 3 casts them heightened, which is exactly the "including a lower-rank spell heightened to 3rd level" clause. Same unenforceable school restriction as Ornate Tattoo.

name: Chosen of Lamashtu
evidence: "Choose one goblin heritage that you do not already have; you gain that heritage and its benefits."
restriction: Must be a goblin heritage you do NOT already have — exclude build.heritageId from the list.
effect: You gain that heritage and ALL its benefits — resistances, senses, granted unarmed Strikes, speeds, granted feats, etc.
engineNote: No second-heritage lane. Character carries a single heritageId and every grant loop reads db.heritages[c.heritageId] only (deriveSpeeds, senses/resistances, innateSpells, grantedStrikes). EffectGrant can hand-express a subset (resistances / senses / skills / innateSpells) but NOT grantedStrikes (Razortooth's jaws), speeds, grantsFeats or loreChoices — so hand-authoring eight EffectGrants would silently drop several heritages' real benefits. Cleanest fix is a `secondHeritageId` on BuildState that the existing heritage grant loops also read.

name: Adroit Manipulation
evidence: "You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Thievery)."
openSource: any skill — but the prompt only appears when the character is ALREADY trained in Thievery

effect: Trains you in Thievery, or in a skill of your choice if Thievery was already trained.
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['adroit-manipulation'] = { skills: { thievery: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }, which is exactly the already-trained→replacement-skill lane (pick stored at `<featId>:fallback:<skill>`). Verified correct against the text. The second sentence ("If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead") is in-play and needs no field.

name: Magaambyan Attendant Dedication
evidence: "When you gain this feat, choose to affiliate with the Cascade Bearers, Emerald Boughs, Rain-Scribes, Tempest-Sun Mages, or Uzunjati. This grants you additional feats available to only that branch."
restriction: Chosen once, when the feat is taken.

engineNote: THREE separate choices live in this one record; only one is currently handled. (a) BRANCH — the spec above; it should gate the 10 branch feats that core.json currently offers unconditionally: cascade-bearers-flexibility, cascade-bearers-spellcasting, emerald-boughs-accustomation, emerald-boughs-hideaway, rain-scribe-sustenance, rain-scribe-mobility, tempest-sun-redirection, tempest-sun-shielding, uzunjati-storytelling, uzunjati-recollection. No feat-gating-by-sibling-choice lane exists. (b) CANTRIP + TRADITION — "cast a single arcane or primal cantrip of your choice… you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability if you choose arcane or Wisdom… if you choose primal". The record has NO spellcastingGrant, and spellcastingGrant is a fixed { tradition, keyAbility, proficiency } object — here both fields follow the pick, so this needs either a choice-driven spellcastingGrant or two options each carrying their own. (c) SKILL — already shipped as FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['magaambyan-attendant-dedication'] = { skillChoices: [{ options: ['arcana','nature'], rank: 'trained' }] }, but it DROPS the upgrade clause "or an expert in one of those skills in which you were already trained"; skillChoices[].conditionalRank: { base: 'trained', upgraded: 'expert' } already exists and should be added.

name: Spell Mastery
evidence: "Select any four spells of 9th rank or lower that are in your spellbook; each spell you select must be of a different rank. These spells are automatically prepared when you make your daily preparations, and you gain an extra spell slot for each spell."
openSource: the character's OWN spellbook (build.spells for the wizard entry), restricted to rank ≤ 9
restriction: Four picks, each of a DIFFERENT rank — a cross-pick validator, not a per-pick filter. Retrainable with 1 week of downtime.
effect: Each mastered spell is auto-prepared at daily preparation AND adds one extra spell slot of that spell's rank.
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) No picker sources from the character's own spellbook — SpellChoiceFilter searches all content spells by tradition/rank and has no 'from your spellbook' mode. (2) SpellSlotBonus only expresses { perRank, exceptHighest, entryId }; here the extra slot must land on each PICKED spell's rank (four specific, distinct ranks), which the shape cannot say. Needs a per-rank slot grant plus a distinct-rank constraint across the four picks.

name: Syncretism
evidence: "Choose a second deity… If you are a cloistered cleric, select one of that deity's domains, gaining the benefits of the Expanded Domain Initiate feat with that domain. If you are a warpriest, you gain the favored weapon of that deity as a second favored weapon…"
openSource: any deity in content.deities (485 records)
restriction: You must meet their alignment requirements and are subject to their edicts and anathema (narrative, not enforceable). A SECOND, DEPENDENT pick follows for cloistered clerics — one of that deity's domains (kind: 'domains', flag 'syncretismDomain', resolved from the chosen deity's `domains` array, not from build.deityId).
effect: Cloistered cleric → the chosen domain's focus spell, Domain-Initiate style (+1 focus point). Warpriest → that deity's favored weapon counts as a second favored weapon, inheriting feats such as Deadly Simplicity.
engineNote: choice.kind: 'domains' resolves its options from build.deityId ONLY — Builder.tsx reads `content.deities[id]?.domains` for the character's own deity and even re-validates featChoices against that list when the deity changes, so a domain picked off a SECOND deity would be silently rewritten. Needs a dependent-choice lane (pick A constrains pick B). The underlying data is all present: deity records carry both `domains` and `favoredWeapons`. The doctrine branch (cloistered vs warpriest) also has to select which half of the effect applies.

name: Divine Access
evidence: "Choose one deity who grants one of your mystery's granted domains. Add up to three cleric spells of your choice granted by that deity to your spell list."
openSource: deities whose `domains` intersect the character's oracle mystery's related domains
restriction: A SECOND, DEPENDENT pick follows: up to three cleric spells granted by that deity (flag 'divineAccessSpells', picks 3, source = that deity's cleric spell list). Repeatable — the same spell may not be chosen twice, but a different domain or a different deity with the same domain may.
effect: The chosen spells are added to the oracle's spell list, making them legal picks when adding or swapping spells in the repertoire.
engineNote: Three blockers, all verified. (1) The mystery→related-domains mapping is PROSE only: d.mystery records are bare stubs ({id, name, edition}) and the oracle class's subclass options keep it inside `description` as "**Related Domains** death, duty, family, soul" — they carry structured grantedSpells / focusSpells / advancedFocusSpell but no domains array. (2) Deity records have `domains`, `divineFont`, `favoredWeapons` and `skill` but NO cleric-spell list, so "cleric spells… granted by that deity" is unresolvable. (3) There is no 'add spells to your spell list' lane — the repertoire picker filters strictly by tradition. SEPARATE DEFECT: the description carries "Special You can select this feat more than once" but the record has no `maxTakable`, which means once. It should be maxTakable: null.

name: Perpetual Breadth
evidence: "Choose a research field. Add one item from the list of options available to that field from perpetual infusions, or two items if you choose your own field."
restriction: A SECOND, DEPENDENT pick follows: 1 item from that field's perpetual-infusion list (2 if you chose your own field), plus a further item if you have Perpetual Potency or Perpetual Perfection.

engineNote: Perpetual infusions are not modeled anywhere: a case-insensitive grep for /perpetual/ across src returns ZERO hits, and the `perpetual-infusions` classFeature in core.json is description-only. The alchemy lane that does exist (PlayState.alchemyPrep / AlchemyPanel, Advanced-Alchemy daily prep + Quick-Alchemy vial spend) has no free-infusion list to extend, and there are no per-field item tables anywhere in the data. This is a subsystem to build, not a field to add — the choice cannot do anything until it exists.

name: Ancestral Weaponry
evidence: "Choose an ancestry for which you have access to all weapons with that trait. For you, melee weapons with that ancestry trait and either the agile or finesse trait gain the monk trait."
restriction: The text requires that you already have access to all weapons with that ancestry trait (the prerequisite names "a feat granting access to all weapons with an ancestry trait (such as elf or orc)"). The app cannot verify this — the weapon-familiarity feats are stored in FEAT_GRANTS.weaponFamiliarity as explicit weapon-id lists, not as an 'access to trait X' flag. Options below are the 18 ancestries that actually have weapons carrying their trait in core.json.
effect: Every melee weapon with that ancestry trait AND the agile or finesse trait gains the `monk` trait for you — so it counts as a monk weapon for Monastic Weaponry, monk stances, and any feature that keys off monk weapons.
engineNote: No 'add a trait to a class of weapons' lane. weaponOverrides / FeatGrant.weaponFamiliarity handle PROFICIENCY for named weapons; the monk trait is a different axis (it drives which Strikes monk features apply to). Needs a weaponTraitGrant-style rider — { addTrait: 'monk', match: { traits: ['<ancestry>'], anyTraits: ['agile','finesse'], melee: true } } — read by deriveStrike when it assembles a weapon's trait list.
question: Should the Ancestral Weaponry ancestry list offer all 18 ancestries that have trait-bearing weapons, or only ancestries the character demonstrably has weapon access to? The latter requires modeling 'access to ALL weapons with trait X' as a flag on the weapon-familiarity feats, which today store explicit weapon-id lists instead.

name: Additional Shadow Magic
evidence: "Choose an additional shadowdancer focus spell you haven't already selected from Shadow Magic. Increase the number of Focus Points in your pool by 1."
restriction: Must NOT be the spell already chosen for Shadow Magic — a cross-record exclusion that is currently unenforced.

engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED as effectChoices with grant.focusSpells, and the focus accounting is correct here — the record deliberately has NO focusPoolBonus because build.ts counts poolMax as featFocusSpells.length + featPoolBonus, so the granted spell already supplies its own point (contrast Universal Versatility above, where adding a grant alongside focusPoolBonus would double-count). Remaining gap: nothing prevents picking the same spell chosen for `shadow-magic:shadowdancer-spell`, which silently yields a duplicate focus spell and only two options exist, so the collision is likely. Needs an option-exclusion keyed to another record's stored pick.

name: Jalmeri Heavenseeker Dedication
evidence: "You gain the Qi Spells monk feat, which grants you a qi spell and a focus pool of 1 Focus Point… If you already have the Qi Spells feat, you can instead choose a single 1st‐level monk feat."
openSource: class feats of level ≤ 1 carrying the `monk` trait — a FEAT_PICK_GRANTS entry { prompt: 'Choose a monk feat', category: 'class', maxLevel: 1, traits: ['monk'] }
restriction: CONDITIONAL — this picker must appear ONLY when the character already owns qi-spells; otherwise the feat simply grants Qi Spells.

(b) BUT `qi-spells` itself has NO choice — its text is "You gain Inner Upheaval, Qi Rush, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell you have access to" and the record has neither `choice`, nor `effectChoices`, nor a FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS entry, so the focus spell it grants is never actually picked. Fixing this dedication therefore requires fixing the separate qi-spells record first. (c) The conditional swap has no lane at all: FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS and FEAT_PICK_GRANTS are both unconditional tables with no 'only if the character lacks X' predicate. (d) Skill half already ships as FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS { skillChoices: [{ options: ['acrobatics','occultism'], rank: 'trained' }] } but DROPS "if you were already trained in both these skills, you become an expert in one of them instead" — add conditionalRank: { base: 'trained', upgraded: 'expert' }.

name: Magical Master
openSource: Any spell of the eidolon's tradition (the tradition is fixed by the chosen eidolon type — angel/demon/psychopomp/undead = divine, construct/dragon = arcane, beast/elemental/fey/plant/swarm = primal, phantoms = occult)

Needs: (a) an eidolon/companion innate-spell field, (b) a spellFilter whose `traditions` resolve dynamically from build.archetypeEidolonType / the summoner subclass option's `tradition`, and (c) exclusion of ranks already filled by Magical Adept (which itself carries no choice field today — magical-adept has choice:null and effectChoices:null, so its 1st+2nd rank picks are also missing).
evidence: "Choose an innate spell of your eidolon's tradition of each of the spell ranks from 1 to 7 in which your eidolon doesn't currently have an innate spell from Magical Adept. Your eidolon can cast each once per day as innate spells."

name: Summoner Dedication
openSource: Any skill (one replacement per eidolon-listed skill you were already trained in)
restriction: Only triggers for eidolon-listed skills the character already has trained; up to 2 (each eidolon type lists exactly 2 skills)
effect: Trained in the eidolon type's two listed skills (angel = Diplomacy+Religion, beast = Intimidation+Nature, construct = Arcana+Crafting, …); each one already trained converts into a free 'different skill of your choice' training.
engineNote: The eidolon TYPE pick is already modeled (BuildState.archetypeEidolonType + a builder picker in shared.tsx:2830, and casterArchetypes 'summoner-dedication' eidolonTradition:true). What is missing is the skill training: build.ts:1221 applies `o.grants.skills` only for `grantOptions` = [subOption, subOption2, ...extraOptions], i.e. CLASS subclass options — the archetype eidolon type never reaches it. FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS has NO 'summoner-dedication' entry at all. `redundantFallback` exists but keys off a STATIC FeatGrant.skills map, and here the two skills depend on build.archetypeEidolonType, so it needs a dynamic-source variant (or per-eidolon-type entries under FeatGrant.choiceGrants keyed by the eidolon id).
evidence: "Choose an eidolon type. You become trained in your eidolon's listed skills. For each of those skills that you are already trained in, you become trained in a different skill of your choice."

name: Cathartic Mage Dedication
restriction: One emotion, fixed for the character (no retraining clause in the text)
effect: Sets the Catharsis reaction's trigger + activation, the Emotional Fervor benefits (including a spell you may cast from a slot while in fervor), the Emotional Fallout, and which focus spell the Cathartic Focus Spell feat later grants. All of those are play-time text; the pick itself is the durable build-time record.
engineNote: Expressible today with `choice` (kind 'array'). IMPORTANT DUPLICATION BUG: the 10-option emotion list already lives on feats['cathartic-focus-spell'].effectChoices (id 'catharsis-emotion', each option granting the matching focus spell — anger→athletic-rush, awe→dazzling-flash, …). That is the WRONG owner: the dedication is where the emotion is chosen. As shipped, a player is asked twice and the two picks can contradict. Fix = put the choice on the dedication and have cathartic-focus-spell READ it (cross-feat choice reference — that part IS engine work) rather than re-ask. The dedication's cantrip grant is already handled by its own effectChoices entry 'cathartic-cantrip'.
evidence: "Choose an emotion to be your catharsis emotion." (record's option list recovered from feats['cathartic-focus-spell'].effectChoices, since this record's description is truncated at "**Emotional States:**")

name: Shadow Reservoir
prompt: Spell source for your shadow reservoir
openSource: The character's own spellcasting entries (class spellcasting, dual-class spellcasting, caster-archetype spellcasting) — a DYNAMIC list, not a fixed one
restriction: Only offered when the character has more than one slot-casting source; otherwise auto-resolves to the single source
effect: Fixes which spell list/slot pool the reservoir draws from and spends.
engineNote: Two separate gaps. (1) The source pick needs options resolved from the built character's spellcasting entries at build time — FeatChoiceDef.kind only supports 'array' (static options) and 'domains' (deity-derived); a 'spellcastingSources' kind (or an EffectChoice with a dynamic option source) would be new. (2) The reservoir CONTENTS (one spell of each rank ≤ highest-castable-rank − 2, from your list, requiring an attack roll or save, castable spontaneously out of a matching slot) is a whole sub-repertoire HH has no representation for — SpellcastingEntry models prepared/repertoire lists, not a parallel reservoir.
question: The text never says WHO picks the reservoir spells or WHEN ('Your shadow reservoir contains a single spell of each spell rank…') — is the reservoir a player-authored list fixed at build time, a daily-preparation list, or should HH just show the rule as prose and model only the source pick?
evidence: "If you have more than one source of spells you can cast with spell slots, such as if you're a spellcaster with a multiclass archetype, choose one source of spells for your shadow reservoir."

name: Soulforger Dedication

options.label: Adaptable Persona (armor only) — climb/swim Speed (fly at 8th)
Bounding Spirit (melee weapon only) — thrown 30 ft + returning
Determined Toughness — condition status penalties reduced by 1
Harmful Malice — +1d4 void damage, innate harm
Heroic Heart — +1 status to attacks, Perception, skills, saves
Healing Grace — fast healing, innate heal
Magical Resilience (armor/shield only) — +2 status to saves & AC vs spells
Planar Bond (armor/shield only) — resistance to a chosen damage type
Planar Pain (weapon only) — Strikes deal a chosen damage type +2
Pull of Stasis (weapon only) — hits slow the target
Reflecting Spirit (armor/shield only) — +2 status AC vs ranged
Resolute Defiance (shield only) — +2 Hardness, temp HP, Shield Block

restriction: The essence power must be legal for the chosen armament type (Armor only / Shield only / Weapon only / Melee weapon only tags in the list). Changing it later costs 1 week of retraining.
effect: Grants a soulforged armament (armor, shield, or weapon) plus the Manifest Soulforged Armament activity; the essence power is a temporary buff applied when you manifest the essence form, and it carries a corruption flaw that only bites while you have soulforged corruption.
engineNote: This record needs TWO choices, so it should use `effectChoices` (an array — core-attunement already carries two entries) rather than the single `choice` field: (1) armament type ['armor','shield','weapon'], (2) the essence power above. `EffectChoice.options[].grant` is optional, so play-time-only powers are legal as bare records. A few grants ARE expressible: adaptable-persona → EffectGrant.speeds, planar-bond → resistances (but the damage type is a NESTED choice — acid/cold/electricity/fire/sonic/spirit/vitality/void — which EffectGrant cannot nest), harmful-malice / healing-grace / magical-resilience → innateSpells. NOT expressible: flat status bonuses to Intimidation/attacks/saves/AC (heroic-heart, deep-seeded-fear, magical-resilience, reflecting-spirit), fast healing, condition-penalty reduction, extra damage dice. Also no predicate exists to gate option (2) on the answer to option (1). Consider the existing Modes system (src/rules/modes.ts) for the manifested-essence buff since it is a toggled state, not a permanent one.
evidence: "You manifest an armor, shield, or weapon as a soulforged armament. Choose one essence power for the armament… Your soulforged armament has an essence power you choose when you first bind it… Essence powers that only apply to some types of armament indicate which."

name: Soul Arsenal
restriction: Must be a DIFFERENT type than the one already chosen for Soulforger Dedication (and, on the second take at 12th+, the one remaining type is forced). Each take also needs its own essence power, legal for that type.
effect: Adds a second (and, on the second take, third) soulforged armament with its own essence power; lets Manifest Soulforged Armament summon any number of them and dismiss them individually; on soulforged corruption you pick which armament's flaw applies at stage 1.
engineNote: maxTakable:2 is already set. Gaps: (a) two choices per take (type + essence power) — again a case for `effectChoices` rather than the single `choice` field; (b) cross-record exclusion — the options must subtract the type picked on soulforger-dedication and on the earlier take of this same feat. FeatChoice stores one `{value,label}` per taken instance, so per-take storage works, but no exclusion predicate exists. A cheap approximation with today's fields: `choice` kind 'array' listing all three types and let the builder show a warning rather than block; the second take at 12th could be auto-resolved (only one type is left).
evidence: "Choose an additional soulforged armament of a different type than the type you already chose, and choose one essence power for it… **Special** You can select this feat a second time at 12th level or higher, choosing the final item type."

name: Dual-Form Weapon
openSource: Any level-0 weapon that is common (or one you have access to)
restriction: Level 0 only; common or accessible; requires a weapon innovation (prerequisites already list 'weapon innovation' and 'expert overdrive')

So there is nothing for a second configuration to hang off, and no place for its second modification set. Needed: an innovation base-weapon field (also missing for the plain Weapon Innovation, whose own text says 'the same statistics as a level 0 simple or martial weapon of your choice'), then a second one plus a second modification set here. A weapon-item picker filtered to level 0 also does not exist as a choice kind (the closest precedent is viking-shieldbearer, which just enumerates two weapon ids).

name: Core Attunement
openSource: Any arcane spell you have access to — one of 5th rank or lower and one of 6th rank or lower

effect: Each chosen spell is castable once per day as an arcane innate spell, in addition to the base 1st-rank and 2nd-rank picks.

Adding the two spellFilter entries without the gate would over-grant.

Needs InventorBuild to accept an archetype-sourced innovationType (mirroring how build.archetypeEidolonType feeds the summoner archetype), with modifications forced empty. Two sub-picks also ride along and have no home for archetype takers: armor innovation's statistics set (build.inventorArmorStats, currently only wired for the class) and weapon innovation's level-0 base weapon (not modeled anywhere at all).

name: Gunslinger Dedication

restriction: You gain the way's skill only — none of its other abilities (no slinger's reload, no deeds). If already trained in that skill, train a skill of your choice instead.

That is lossy in two ways: the WAY itself is never recorded (so Pistolero's Challenge, whose prerequisite is literally 'Way of the Pistolero', can't be validated for an archetype taker), and a player can pick a skill without picking the way it belongs to.
