name: Sniping Duo Dedication
openSource: A willing, non-minion ally — free text, or a party member when the character is in a Campaign
restriction: Not a minion; changing spotters costs 3 days of downtime; every Sniping Duo feat's benefit requires both of you alive and conscious
effect: You and your spotter don't give each other's targets lesser cover, and after either of you hits a target, the other gets +1 circumstance per weapon damage die on their next Strike against it before the end of their next turn.
engineNote: No free-text 'name an ally' choice kind exists (the closest precedent is the background/Lore free-text input via BuildState.backgroundLore and FeatGrant.loreChoices, which is a typed string — the same mechanism would work). The BONUS itself is conditional and reciprocal, so it belongs in the Modes system (a toggled '+1 per damage die, spotter hit this target' mode) rather than a static grant. HH's Campaigns/Party feature could supply a real teammate list instead of free text.
question: Should ally-designation feats (this, and Vehicle Mechanic's shared vehicle) use a free-text field, or bind to a real campaign teammate now that Campaigns/Party exists?
evidence: "When you take this dedication, choose one willing, non-minion ally to act as your spotter… You can change your designated spotter by spending 3 days of downtime training with another ally."

name: Dongun Education
restriction: Exactly two of the three named Lores (pairs are enumerated so a single `choice` covers a 2-of-3 pick); uncommon, access-gated to Dongun Hold or Alkenstar
effect: Trained in both chosen Lores at 1st level, expert at 2nd, master at 7th, legendary at 15th.
engineNote: Fully expressible with fields that already exist, no engine change: `choice` kind 'array' with the three pairs above, plus FEAT_GRANTS['dongun-education'] = { choiceGrants: { 'engineering-explosive': { skills: { 'lore:engineering':'trained', 'lore:explosive':'trained' } }, … }, rankUpgrade: [{level:2,rank:'expert'},{level:7,rank:'master'},{level:15,rank:'legendary'}] }. FeatGrant.skills is keyed by ProficiencyKey (= SkillId | `lore:${string}`) so Lore keys are legal there; note that `skillChoices.options` is typed SkillId[] and canNOT hold Lore skills, which is exactly why the pair-enumeration route is the right one. rankUpgrade applies to everything the feat grants, which is correct here since it grants nothing else. Confirm the Lore slugs HH already uses (the AoN-verification pass added ~40 Lore skills) so 'lore:engineering' / 'lore:explosive' / 'lore:firearm' match existing keys.
evidence: "Pick two of the following Lore skills: Engineering Lore, Explosive Lore, or Firearm Lore. At 2nd level, you gain expert proficiency in these Lore skills; at 7th level, you gain master proficiency in these Lore skills; and at 15th level, you gain legendary proficiency in them."

name: Captivator Dedication
openSource: Occult cantrips from the enchantment or illusion school
restriction: Occult list; enchantment or illusion school only; granted as at-will innate spells with Charisma as the key attribute and trained occult spell attack/DC
effect: Two at-will occult innate cantrips + the Cast a Spell activity + trained occult spell attack rolls and DCs (key attribute Charisma).
engineNote: Two items. (1) The cantrip picks belong in `effectChoices` with a spellFilter { traditions:['occult'], cantripsOnly:true, grantAs:'innate', innate:{ tradition:'occult', atWill:true } } — the same shape cathartic-mage-dedication already uses. The blocker is the SCHOOL restriction: core.json spells carry no `school` field and post-Remaster school traits are almost entirely stripped (only 4 spells anywhere have the 'enchantment' trait; occult cantrips carrying enchantment/illusion are just musical-accompaniment, figment, message, bullhorn, ghost-sound), so `SpellChoiceFilter.traits:['enchantment']` would return a near-empty list. Fix is either a `school` field on Spell or an explicit enumerated option list for the captivator feats. (2) SEPARATE DATA BUG, no engine work needed: FEAT_SKILL_GRANTS['captivator-dedication'] is `skillChoices:[{options:['deception','diplomacy'],rank:'trained'}]` and silently drops the upgrade clause — it should carry `conditionalRank:{ base:'trained', upgraded:'expert' }`, a field that already exists (see lion-blade-dedication).
evidence: "Choose Deception or Diplomacy. You become trained in that skill, or become an expert if you were already trained. Choose two cantrips from the occult list; each cantrip must be from either the enchantment or illusion school… you can cast these spells as occult innate spells."

name: Basic Captivator Spellcasting
openSource: Occult spells from the enchantment or illusion school
restriction: One 1st-rank spell now, one 2nd-rank spell at 6th level, one 3rd-rank spell at 8th level; every one must be occult and enchantment or illusion
effect: Each chosen spell is castable once per day as an occult innate spell (Charisma key attribute, from the dedication).
engineNote: Structurally this is the core-attunement pattern and maps cleanly onto three `effectChoices` entries with spellFilters — { traditions:['occult'], rank:1, grantAs:'innate', innate:{tradition:'occult',usesPerDay:1} }, then rank:2 with minLevel:6, then rank:3 with minLevel:8 (SpellChoiceFilter.minLevel exists exactly for scaling picks). The ONLY blocker is the same school restriction as captivator-dedication — no `school` field on Spell — so without it the picker would offer every occult spell of that rank. Note this feat is NOT a spell-slot archetype (no Basic/Expert/Master slot progression); it is innate-only, so it must not be wired into casterArchetypes.
evidence: "Choose a 1st-rank occult spell from either the enchantment or illusion school. You can Cast this Spell as an occult innate spell. At 6th level, you gain a 2nd-rank spell, and at 8th level, you gain a 3rd-rank spell."

name: Heightened Captivation
openSource: The spells the character was granted by captivator archetype feats (Captivator Dedication's cantrips, Basic Captivator Spellcasting's picks, …) — a DYNAMIC list derived from other feats' choices
restriction: Cannot be from your highest rank of non-cantrip captivator spells; cannot be changed later; repeatable (maxTakable:null) and each take must be a different spell
effect: That spell is permanently heightened to the highest rank of non-cantrip captivator spell you can cast.
engineNote: Needs two things HH lacks. (1) A choice whose options come from other feats' resolved picks — no such kind exists (FeatChoiceDef is static; EffectChoice is static options or an open spellFilter). Provenance IS partly available: the 'per-source spell attribution' work already tags where a spell came from, so a filter of 'innate spells whose source feat has archetype === captivator' is the natural query. (2) A per-spell heighten override on an innate grant: InnateSpellGrant has `rank`, `heightenHalfLevel` and `heightenAt`, but none of them expresses 'match my highest captivator spell rank', and none can be applied retroactively to a spell granted by a DIFFERENT feat. Also needs the 'not your highest rank' exclusion and cross-take de-duplication.
evidence: "Choose one of your spells granted by captivator archetype feats; this spell can't be from your highest level of non-cantrip captivator spells… You can't later change the spell that is heightened by this feat. **Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, you choose a different spell."

name: Spell Trickster Dedication
restriction: Exactly the seven 4th-level spell trickster archetype feats (verified against core.json: no others exist at that level); you may only take one whose spellcasting prerequisite you meet ('ability to cast X'); the normal level prerequisite is ignored, and these two do NOT count toward the two-feats-before-a-new-dedication rule
effect: Grants those two feats (each a permanent modification you may apply to the named spell when you cast it) at 2nd level.
engineNote: This is a FEAT_PICK_GRANTS case with `ids` set to the seven ids above — except FEAT_PICK_GRANTS supports exactly ONE pick per granting feat (BuildState.pickFeatChoices is Record<featId, string>, and build.ts:2019 reads a single value). Two picks needs the map to become Record<featId, string[]> (or a keyed `<featId>:<slot>` scheme like featSkillChoices already uses). Second gap: the 'ability to cast <spell>' prerequisite is free text in `prerequisites` — filtering the picker to spells the character can actually cast needs the picker to consult the built spell list. Third: this dedication overrides the archetype-progression rule (canTakeNewDedication in build.ts counts non-dedication archetype feats — the two granted ones must be excluded).
evidence: "Choose up to two 4th-level spell trickster archetype feats for which you meet the spell-casting prerequisite. You gain those feats, ignoring their level prerequisite."

name: Shield Augmentation

options.label: Thrown 10 feet (choose two from this group)
Versatile S (choose two from this group)

restriction: EITHER exactly one of {backswing, forceful} OR exactly two of {disarm, nonlethal, shove, thrown-10, trip, versatile-s}. The two groups can never be mixed, and 'picks' is therefore 1 or 2 depending on the branch. The pick is permanent — made when the augmentation is created — and the augmented shield can't also carry an attached weapon such as shield spikes.
evidence: "A shield augmentation grants your shield one or more weapon traits, chosen when the augmentation is created."
effect: Adds the chosen weapon trait(s) to the shield the augmentation is applied to (usage 'applied-to-shield'), affecting its shield-bash Strike. It otherwise leaves the shield's statistics alone, and the augmentation can still be etched with weapon runes.
engineNote: THREE gaps, all real. (1) No per-INSTANCE storage: item picks live in BuildState.effectChoices keyed `<itemId>:<choiceId>` (src/rules/build.ts ~2389), so two augmented shields would silently share one pick; needs a per-InventoryItem choice map next to heldSpell/runes/attachedTo. (2) No grant kind for this effect: EffectGrant carries resistances/weaknesses/immunities/senses/speeds/skills/spells/focus/ItemPassiveEffects — nothing that adds WEAPON TRAITS to another inventory item. The existing drag-to-attach lane (planAttach + InventoryItem.attachedTo) is the natural host, so the grant would need to read attachedTo and merge traits into the target shield's Strike. (3) EffectChoice holds a single string value, so it cannot express a two-pick or a mutually-exclusive group; either add a multi-pick EffectChoice or store the pick as one composite value (e.g. 'disarm+trip').

name: Ancestral Embrace
openSource: Any ancestry feat of the WEARER'S OWN ancestry — i.e. content.feats filtered to category === 'ancestry' and matching build.ancestryId (plus versatile-heritage feats the character already qualifies for). Do not enumerate; the pool is the same one the ancestry-feat slot picker already uses, with the level cap removed.
restriction: Any level (the feat's own level is explicitly ignored), but all OTHER prerequisites must be met. Re-choosable: a different feat may be selected each time the armor is invested, and the feat is lost when investment ends.
evidence: "You gain an ancestry feat from your ancestry; the feat can be any level, but you must meet any other prerequisites of the feat."
effect: While the armor is invested, the character gains the chosen ancestry feat and everything that feat itself grants (proficiencies, strikes, innate spells, further granted feats). It should appear in the feat list tagged as granted by the item, and disappear when the armor is un-invested.
engineNote: No existing lane fits. Item.grantsFeats is a FIXED string[] (The Survivor → Diehard), and EffectGrant has no feat field at all, so a chosen feat can't be routed through effectChoices either. The pick-a-feat machinery DOES exist for feats (src/rules/featPickGrants.ts + FEAT_GRANTS, used by General Training / Basic-X), so the work is: (a) let an ITEM declare an open feat pick and reuse that picker, filtered to the wearer's ancestry with prerequisite validation but NO level cap; (b) per-instance storage — BuildState.effectChoices is keyed by item DEFINITION id, and InventoryItem has no choice map; (c) gate the grant on invested === true, which is new — granted feats are unconditional today; (d) make the granted feat transitive, since ancestry feats can themselves grant feats. The other two activations (an extra daily use of a limited ancestry feat; shortening a legend lore ritual) are in-play and need nothing.

name: Kineticist Dedication
restriction: Exactly one element. Values deliberately match the kineticist class's own extraChoices group id 'element' (air-gate…wood-gate) so the existing gate-junction data is reused.
effect: Sets the archetype character's kinetic element: it decides the Elemental Blast damage type/traits, the kinetic aura, and which impulse feats are legal later (Add Element, Advanced Element Control). The chosen gate option in classes.kineticist.extraChoices already carries its junction text and its Skill Junction grant (e.g. air-gate → stealth).
evidence: "Choose one element to be your kinetic element (air, earth, fire, metal, water, or wood)."
engineNote: The element picker and its junction machinery in src/builder/shared.tsx are gated on ownsClass('kineticist') and read build.extraChoices['element']; a non-kineticist who takes the dedication stores nothing, so the archetype has no element at all. Needs an archetype-side store (mirroring build.archetypeEidolonType / archetypeTradition) that the same gate code can read. The feat's OTHER clause ('trained in Nature; if already trained, another skill of your choice') is ALREADY handled — featGrantsAuto.ts has `'kineticist-dedication': { skills: { nature: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }`.

name: Add Element
restriction: Must be an element you do NOT already have (exclude the one picked for Kineticist Dedication and any earlier Add Element).
effect: Adds a second kinetic element, AND grants a bonus impulse feat for that element (prerequisites checked against half your character level). Also unlocks hybrid impulses that require both elements.
evidence: "Choose a second kinetic element to add to the one you already have. You gain an impulse feat for that element."
engineNote: TWO picks, not one: element + bonus impulse feat. Both shapes already exist for the CLASS path — build.gateForks (Fork the Path: new element, keyed by threshold level, filtered against already-owned elements) and build.gateExpands (Expand the Portal: bonus impulse feat, filtered to `traits.includes('impulse') && level <= L` and element-trait match). Reuse both, keyed on the archetype element store rather than build.extraChoices['element']. The FeatChoiceDef `choice` field can only carry the first pick; the impulse pick needs the gateExpands-style secondary picker.

name: Otherworldly Acumen
openSource: any common 2nd-rank spell from the SAME tradition as an innate spell you already gained from another elf ancestry feat
restriction: Rank exactly 2; common rarity only; tradition must match an innate spell already granted by another elf ancestry feat (arcane if that feat was Otherworldly Magic).
effect: Grants the chosen spell as an innate spell, castable once per day, using that tradition.
evidence: "Choose one common 2nd-rank spell from the same tradition as an innate spell you previously gained from another elf ancestry feat … You can cast that spell as an innate spell once per day"
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — this record carries effectChoices[0] = { id:'acumen-spell', spellFilter:{ traditions:[arcane,divine,occult,primal], rank:2, cantripsOnly:false, grantAs:'innate', innate:{usesPerDay:1} } }, and src/rules/spellChoice.ts resolves it. Two known permissivenesses, both harmless-but-wrong: (a) all four traditions are offered instead of the one matching your existing elf-feat innate spell (that dependency can't be expressed — SpellChoiceFilter has no 'same tradition as another grant' field); (b) SpellChoiceFilter has no rarity field, so uncommon/rare 2nd-rank spells are offered despite the text saying "common".

name: Adapted Cantrip
openSource: any cantrip whose tradition list does NOT include your class's spellcasting tradition
restriction: Cantrips only (rank 0); must come from a tradition other than your own; requires a spellcasting class feature. Retrainable to a different alternate tradition later.
effect: Prepared casters may prepare the chosen cantrip in addition to their normal options; repertoire casters replace one known cantrip with it. It is cast as a spell of YOUR class's tradition, using your class spell attack/DC — not as an innate spell.
evidence: "Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own. … You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition."
engineNote: No lane fits. SpellChoiceFilter.grantAs only supports 'innate' | 'focus'; granting as 'innate' would be wrong (innate casting is a separate entry with its own attribute/DC, and it would not be swappable/heightenable as a class cantrip). Needs (a) a new grantAs like 'classCantrip' that injects into the character's class spell entry, and (b) a dynamic 'exclude my own tradition' filter clause, since the legal set depends on the class chosen elsewhere in the build.

name: Unconventional Weaponry
openSource: uncommon simple or martial weapons that carry an ancestry trait or are culturally specific — upgraded to uncommon ADVANCED weapons if you are trained in all martial weapons
restriction: Uncommon rarity; ancestry-traited or another culture's weapon. In shipped data: 33 uncommon simple/martial weapons carry an ancestry trait (clan-dagger, dogslicer, elven-curve-blade, horsechopper, halfling-sling-staff, tengu-gale-blade …) out of 443 uncommon simple/martial weapons total; 25 uncommon advanced weapons carry an ancestry trait.
effect: Grants ACCESS to the chosen weapon and treats it as a simple weapon for proficiency (so it uses your simple-weapon rank) — or, in the advanced-weapon branch, as a martial weapon.
evidence: "Choose an uncommon simple or martial weapon with a trait corresponding to an ancestry (such as dwarf, goblin, or orc) or that is common in another culture. You gain access to that weapon, and for the purpose of proficiency, you treat it as a simple weapon."
engineNote: FEAT_GRANTS.weaponFamiliarity is the closest lane but takes a STATIC weapon list plus a flat rank or mirrorBestCategory; there is no lane for a player-CHOSEN weapon, and no lane for 'treat this specific weapon as category X' (mirrorBestCategory mirrors the BEST category rank, which is too generous — it would give a martial-trained character martial rank on the advanced branch even before they qualify). Also needs the level/trained-in-all-martials branch to swap the offered pool.
question: "or that is common in another culture" has no machine-readable tag. Should the picker offer only the 33 ancestry-traited uncommon simple/martial weapons (rules-tight, may block legitimate cultural weapons), or all 443 uncommon simple/martial weapons (permissive, matches the GM-adjudicated intent)?

name: Adaptive Adept
openSource: any cantrip or 1st-rank spell from the SAME tradition you chose for Adapted Cantrip
restriction: Rank 0 or 1 only; tradition must equal the tradition of the Adapted Cantrip pick. If a 1st-rank spell is chosen you gain no access to its heightened versions (can't prepare them, can't learn them, can't make it a signature spell).
effect: Adds the chosen spell to your spell options exactly like the Adapted Cantrip pick; cast as a spell of your class's tradition.
evidence: "Choose a cantrip or 1st-rank spell from the same magical tradition as your cantrip from Adapted Cantrip. You gain that spell, adding it to your spell options just like the cantrip from Adapted Cantrip."
engineNote: Depends on ANOTHER feat's pick (Adapted Cantrip's tradition) — SpellChoiceFilter has no way to reference a sibling choice, so the option source must be computed at build time. Shares Adapted Cantrip's missing 'add to class spell list' grant (grantAs is only 'innate'|'focus'). The no-heightened-versions caveat also has no lane. Should be built together with adapted-cantrip.

name: Scion of Many Planes
openSource: any 1st-level nephilim lineage feat you do not already possess
restriction: Must not already be possessed. Shipped pool = the 16 level-1 feats with traits ['nephilim','lineage'] (angelkin, grimspawn, hellspawn, lawbringer, musetouched, pitborn, aeonbound, battleblooded, faultspawn, proteankin, emberkin, idyllkin, plumekith, beastbrood, riftmarked, shackleborn). garudas-squall also carries both traits but is level 5 and requires Plumekith — a lineage FOLLOW-UP, not a base lineage; a maxLevel of 1 excludes it correctly.
effect: Grants the chosen lineage feat as a bonus feat (no slot consumed) with all of its own effects, transitively.
evidence: "Choose one nephilim lineage feat that you do not already possess; you gain that feat and all of its benefits, even if you already took a lineage feat at 1st level."
engineNote: Pure DATA addition — the lane already exists. Add to FEAT_PICK_GRANTS in src/rules/featPickGrants.ts: `'scion-of-many-planes': { prompt: 'Choose a nephilim lineage feat', category: 'ancestry', maxLevel: 1, traits: ['nephilim', 'lineage'] }`. The pick lands in build.pickFeatChoices and buildCharacter grants it with its effects.

name: Elf Atavism
restriction: Elf heritages only; taken at 1st level only and never retrainable in or out. The text warns you typically can't take a heritage that depends on an elven feature you lack (Ancient Elf's multi-century lifespan being the named example). content.heritages also contains 'aon-half-elf' with ancestryId 'elf' — that is the legacy half-elf heritage and should NOT be offered here.
effect: You gain the benefits of the chosen ELF heritage on top of your aiuvarin heritage (its senses, speeds, skill/feat grants — e.g. Cavern Elf darkvision, Seer Elf innate detect-magic, Ancient Elf's multiclass dedication).
evidence: "You gain the benefits of the elf heritage of your elven parent or ancestors. You typically can't select a heritage that depends on or improves an elven feature you don't have."
engineNote: BuildState has a single heritageId, so there is no slot to hold a SECOND heritage and no code path that applies a second heritage's DefenseGrants/effectChoices. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS already keys an entry off build.heritageId ('ancient-elf'), which is precedent for heritage-driven pickers — but that grants a FEAT, not a whole heritage. Needs a secondary-heritage slot whose grants merge like the primary's. Note the recursion risk: picking Ancient Elf here also drags in its own multiclass-dedication picker.
question: Elf Atavism's legal heritage list is explicitly GM-adjudicated ("at the GM's discretion, you might gain a different benefit"). Offer all 8 elf heritages including Ancient Elf (which chains into a multiclass-dedication picker), or curate the list down to the ones with no elven-feature dependency?

name: Advanced Domain
restriction: Only domains for which you ALREADY have the initial domain spell (i.e. domains you took with Domain Initiate) — not simply every domain your deity offers. maxTakable is null, so it repeats; each taking must yield a different advanced domain spell.
effect: Grants that domain's ADVANCED domain focus spell and expands your focus pool by 1 (focusPoolBonus: 1 is already on the record).
evidence: "You gain an advanced domain spell from one of your domains for which you have an initial domain spell."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) src/rules/domains.ts has only DOMAIN_SPELLS (domain → INITIAL focus spell); there is no ADVANCED_DOMAIN_SPELLS table, so a picked domain resolves to no spell. The advanced spells do ship (competitive-edge, eradicate-undeath, tempest-form …) — this is an authoring job mirroring the existing table. (2) kind:'domains' resolves options from the DEITY's domain list; here the legal set is the subset actually taken via Domain Initiate, so the domains resolver needs a 'restrict to domains you already have an initial spell for' mode.

name: Order Explorer
restriction: Must be an order OTHER than your own (exclude build.subclassId). maxTakable is null — repeatable, and each taking must pick a different order not already explored.
effect: You count as a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites, AND you gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite. You gain none of the order's other benefits (no order spell, no order skill).
evidence: "Choose an order other than your own. You gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite, and you are now a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites."
engineNote: Three parts. (1) The order-membership flag for prerequisite checking has no lane. (2) The granted feat is a SECOND, dependent pick — 'a 1st-level feat whose prerequisite names the order you just chose'. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS filters by category/level/trait only, never by another choice's value, so the pool must be computed at build time. (3) DATA GAP: of the 9 orders, only 7 have a level-1 order-prerequisite feat in core.json (fire-lung/flame, shore-step/wave, steadying-stone/stone, animal-companion/animal, leshy-familiar/leaf, storm-born/storm, untamed-form/untamed). Cultivation and Spore orders have only 6th-level feats (hedge-prison, fungal-exhalation), so picking those two would grant nothing.

name: Order Magic
restriction: Only orders you actually selected with Order Explorer — the static list above is the full superset and MUST be narrowed at build time. maxTakable is null; each taking must pick a different explored order.
effect: Grants that order's INITIAL order focus spell and expands the focus pool by 1 (focusPoolBonus: 1 is already on the record). The mapping already exists in data: classes.druid.subclass.options[].focusSpells — animal→heal-animal, cultivation→cornucopia, flame→wildfire, leaf→cornucopia, spore→mushroom-patch, stone→crushing-ground, storm→tempest-surge, untamed→untamed-shift, wave→rising-surf.
evidence: "Choose an order you have selected with Order Explorer. You gain the initial order spell from that order."
engineNote: The legal option set is the set of Order Explorer picks — a cross-feat dependency that FeatChoiceDef.options (a static array) cannot express. Needs a dynamic option source reading the Order Explorer selections, plus wiring the picked order's focusSpells entry into the focus-spell grant. Build this after order-explorer; alone it would offer orders the character never explored.

name: Advanced Weapon Training
restriction: One weapon group. Values are the 17 ids in content.weaponGroup. The text imposes no restriction, but only 13 groups actually contain advanced weapons in shipped data (axe 5, sword 22, firearm 9, knife 5, club 4, flail 10, crossbow 3, dart 2, sling 3, bow 3, pick 2, spear 1, polearm 2) — bomb, brawling, hammer and shield would be inert picks.
effect: Every ADVANCED weapon in the chosen group uses your MARTIAL weapon proficiency rank instead of your advanced rank (attack rolls, and it feeds crit-spec/rank-scaling the same way).
evidence: "Choose a weapon group. You gain proficiency with all advanced weapons in that group as if they were martial weapons of their weapon group."
engineNote: No lane. BuildState.fighterWeaponGroup exists but is bespoke to Fighter Weapon Mastery/Legend (it pushes a group to master@5/legendary@13). FeatGrant.weaponFamiliarity takes a STATIC weapon list plus a flat rank or mirrorBestCategory — mirrorBestCategory is too generous here (it mirrors the best category rank, not specifically martial). Needs a 'group → treat advanced as martial' override applied through the same weaponOverrides path deriveStrike already reads.

name: Rites of Convocation
openSource: any summon spell that appears on your spellcasting tradition's list
restriction: Must be a 'Summon …' spell on the tradition of your witch spellcasting. 27 summon spells ship, e.g. summon-animal (r1, arcane/primal), summon-construct (r1, arcane), summon-fey (r1, occult/primal), summon-undead (r1, arcane/divine/occult), summon-elemental (r2, arcane/primal), summon-dragon (r5, all four), summon-kaiju (r10, primal).
effect: Names a permanent 'convocation' spell. Thereafter, 10 minutes of communion with your familiar swaps one prepared witch spell for the chosen summon spell, heightened to the replaced slot's rank; the replaced slot must be at least the summon spell's minimum rank.
evidence: "Choose one summon spell (such as Summon Animal, Summon Construct, and so forth) that appears on the spell list of your spellcasting tradition."
engineNote: The PICK is build-time and permanent; the EFFECT is a prepared-slot flexibility the engine cannot express. SpellChoiceFilter.grantAs offers only 'innate' | 'focus' — neither is right (this spell is cast from a witch slot with witch statistics). Also, 'summon spell' is not a trait in the data: the 27 spells are identifiable only by the 'Summon ' name prefix, so the filter needs a name/id list rather than a trait match. Minimum viable = record the pick for display (an EffectChoice option with no grant already supports a grant-less recorded pick).
question: Rites of Convocation's benefit is a 10-minute prepared-slot SWAP, which the spell-slot model does not support. Is recording the chosen summon spell for display (and letting the player do the swap by hand on the Spells page) acceptable, or should a 'flexible swap' lane be built?

name: Library Robes
openSource: Any spell you know (repertoire, prepared list, or otherwise available to you) of 5th rank or lower
restriction: Rank 5 or lower, and it must be a spell the character knows. You must pay the minimum materials to Craft a scroll of that spell (about half a scroll's Price plus any extra cost); no Crafting proficiency and no Magical Crafting feat needed. Re-chosen at each daily preparation, and choosing erases the previous inscription.
effect: Puts a single-use scroll of the chosen spell on the character (naturally the Spells page, as an item-held spell with 1 charge), on top of the robes' baseline +1 resilient scroll robes statistics.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one spell you know of 5th rank or lower. You inscribe that spell on the robes ... Using this ability erases any scroll already inscribed on the robe."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) NO item in core.json currently carries a `choice` field (verified: 0 of the whole items collection), so the choice lane is feats/classFeatures-only today — item-borne choices need an engine path that reads `choice` off an owned item instance and stores the answer per item copy, not per character. (2) The answer must materialise as a one-use spell entry: the app already has `heldSpells` + `inv.counters` charges for staves/wands, so the plumbing exists, but `heldSpells` is a static authored map — it cannot currently be filled from a player answer. (3) The option pool is character-dependent ('a spell you know'), so the picker must read the character's own repertoire/prepared list rather than the global spell list.
question: Library Robes is re-chosen at every daily preparation, not locked at purchase. Should re-selectable daily-prep choices like this live in the builder `choice` lane (answer persisted on the item, editable any time), or in the play state alongside the existing alchemist Advanced-Alchemy daily prep? effect: Narrows which spell the tattoo can cast once per day. The record's `heldSpells` currently lists BOTH harm and heal at rank 1, so today a Sarenrae worshipper (divineFont: ['heal']) is offered Harm from this item — the answer should filter `heldSpells` down to the single chosen/forced spell.

engineNote: Three things. (1) NO item in core.json carries a `choice` field today (verified across the whole items collection), so item-borne choices have no engine lane at all — this is the prerequisite work. That option is picked per activation anyway (in-play), but it can never be shown until deity cleric spell lists are imported.

The `choice` shape holds only one choice per record, so if sanctification is in scope it needs either a second slot or its own field. Same question applies to all four Faith Tattoo grades.

name: The Queen Mother
openSource: any Lore subject — free-text, exactly like Background.trainedLoreChoice (the pick becomes lore:<typed subject>)
restriction: Must be a Lore skill in which you currently have NO proficiency. Re-selectable once per day during daily preparations while the artifact stays invested.
evidence: "When you first invest The Queen Mother, choose a Lore skill in which you have no proficiency... you treat that Lore skill as if your proficiency rank with it were a master."
effect: Sets the chosen Lore's proficiency rank to master, or to legendary if the character is 15th level or higher. This is a rank OVERRIDE, not a bonus — it is the only record in this chunk that changes a derived sheet number.
engineNote: Cannot be expressed today, three ways. (1) There is no free-text/open Lore kind: FeatChoiceDef.kind is only 'domains' | 'array' and EffectChoice.options is a fixed enumeration; the free-text Lore input built for backgrounds (BuildState.backgroundLore) is not reusable from an item. (2) EffectGrant.skills maps to a single flat ProficiencyRank with no level condition, so 'master, legendary at 15th' needs a conditional-rank grant. (3) The 'no existing proficiency' restriction needs a validator that reads the character's current Lore trainings, and the once-per-day swap needs the pick to live in play/daily-prep state rather than the immutable build. Also note: zero items in core.json currently carry a choice or effectChoices field, so this would be the first item-driven builder prompt — the wiring (resolvedItemPassives is described in types.ts but only for worn-item passives) needs checking before data is authored.
question: Where should The Queen Mother's Lore pick live — a one-time builder prompt on the invested item, or a daily-preparations slot that can be re-chosen each day as the rules say? And should the app enforce 'a Lore you have no proficiency in', or just warn? This is the first item in the data that would need a builder-visible choice, so it sets the precedent.

name: Possibility Tome
openSource: …plus "a single subcategory of Lore" — an open free-text Lore subject (the shape Background.trainedLoreChoice uses), which EffectChoice's fixed `options` array cannot express.
restriction: Re-chosen every time the book is activated (10-minute activation); the loaded subject expires after 24 hours or when the tome is activated again.
effect: +3 item bonus to Recall Knowledge checks made with the chosen skill, and a critical failure on such a check becomes a plain failure.
evidence: "Choose one skill: Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or a single subcategory of Lore."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) The bonus is doubly conditional — only on Recall Knowledge, and only if you spend an Interact perusing the book first — while ItemPassiveEffects.skills is a flat bonus to ALL uses of the skill. Granting a flat +3 to Arcana/Crafting/Medicine would be wrong (unlike the accepted `loreBonus` approximation, which the type comment justifies only because Lores are used almost solely for Recall Knowledge). (2) The Lore branch needs a free-text subject input inside EffectChoice. Until both exist, ship the pick with options carrying no `grant` (explicitly allowed: "An option with no grant simply applies nothing") plus a note.
question: Precedent (ancestral-geometry) prompts for a choice that is re-picked at daily preparations, but that item's bonus applies automatically. Possibility Tome's choice only matters after a deliberate 10-minute activation. Do activation-gated, 24-hour choices get a builder prompt at all, or should they live in play-state (Modes) instead?

name: Dweomerveil
restriction: Re-chosen at each daily preparations (requires brushing and oiling the veil); lasts until the next daily preparations. Same pattern as the already-shipped `ancestral-geometry` effectChoice.
effect: +1 item bonus to all saving throws against magic of the chosen tradition, and it defines the Dimension Leap reaction's trigger ("You succeed at a saving throw against a spell from the chosen tradition").
evidence: "At the conclusion of the activity, select one tradition of magic (arcane, divine, occult, or primal). You gain a +1 item bonus to all saves against magic from that tradition".
engineNote: ItemPassiveEffects.saves is a single unconditional number — there is no per-tradition (or any conditional) save-bonus lane, so emitting `passive: { saves: 1 }` would grant +1 to ALL saves and be flatly wrong. Ship the four options with no `grant` (recorded + displayed only) until a conditional-save lane exists; the pick is still needed because it also names the reaction's trigger.

name: Storied Skin
openSource: Any Lore subject — free text, exactly like Background.trainedLoreChoice ("the player types the subject in the builder"). Not a fixed list.
restriction: Chosen once, permanently, when the tattoo is applied — the record says "When you receive the tattoo", and the activation later refers back to "the chosen Lore skill". It is not re-picked.
effect: +1 item bonus to checks with the chosen Lore skill (strictly: when you add the visual trait to Recall Knowledge to study your tattoos). Concretely `passive: { skills: { "lore:<subject>": 1 } }` — the same key shape ancestral-geometry already uses.
evidence: "When you receive the tattoo, choose a Lore skill. … granting you a +1 item bonus to your check using the chosen Lore skill."
engineNote: EffectChoice can only offer a fixed `options` array (or a spellFilter); there is no free-text Lore-subject input on the effect-choice lane — `trainedLoreChoice` exists only on Background. Either add a free-text/lore kind to EffectChoice, or fall back to enumerating a fixed Lore list the way ancestral-geometry does (which would wrongly exclude Lores outside that list). The bonus itself is expressible once the subject is known, and the loreBonus type comment already blesses treating a Recall-Knowledge-only Lore bonus as a flat Lore bonus.

name: Stone of Unrivaled Skill
openSource: Any skill — the text says only "one skill", with no restriction to trained skills and no list, so the pool is all skills (Lore subjects presumably included).
restriction: Chosen once when the bargained contract is sealed; permanent for as long as the contract is invested. Never re-picked.
effect: Raises that skill's proficiency ONE STEP with a floor of expert: untrained/trained → expert, expert → master, master → legendary. The same chosen skill is also what the Taste Fluency activation buffs (+3 status bonus for 10 minutes, once per day).
evidence: "Choose one skill when you seal this bargained contract. You become an expert in that skill; if you were already an expert, you become a master, and if you were already a master, you become legendary."
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) EffectGrant.skills is documented as "Skill (or lore:<subject>) → MINIMUM rank trained", so a hard-coded 'expert' grant would leave an existing expert at expert — this needs a new relative "raise one step (min expert)" grant, which no lane provides. (2) There is no all-skills picker on the choice lanes: EffectChoice takes only a fixed `options` array, and FeatChoiceDef's kind is only 'domains' | 'array' — the 'skills' kind this record needs does not exist yet. This is the single highest-value record in the chunk: it is a permanent, always-on proficiency change that the app currently drops entirely.

name: Muse
restriction: One of the two; "If your relic allows you to do so, you can take this gift again to choose the other" — a second, separate taking, not a second pick inside the same choice.
effect: Item bonus to the chosen skill, scaling with the RELIC's level: +1 at 3rd, +2 once the relic reaches 9th, +3 at 17th.
evidence: "providing an item bonus to Crafting or Performance checks. (Choose one. If your relic allows you to do so, you can take this gift again to choose the other.)"
engineNote: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED but incomplete: the record carries effectChoices `muse-skill` with the correct two options — however both grants hard-code `passive.skills.<skill> = 1`, ignoring the record's own scaling ("Once the relic attains 9th level, the bonus increases to +2. The bonus increases to +3 when the relic is 17th level"). ItemPassiveEffects.skills is a flat number with no level table, and the app has no notion of a relic's level as distinct from the character's. Also unhandled: taking the gift twice (EffectChoice ids are single-pick per record). Verify the shipped choice before adding anything — do not duplicate it.

name: Artistic Perfection
restriction: Exactly one of the two named skills; permanent once the relic gift is gained (no re-pick clause, unlike Muse).
effect: Any success on a check with the chosen skill becomes a critical success.
evidence: "Your relic enhances your skill with Crafting or Performance. (Choose one.) If you succeed at a check with the chosen skill, you get a critical success instead."
engineNote: The pick itself is trivially expressible (two-option EffectChoice, same shape as the sibling `muse` record which already ships one), but the EFFECT is a degree-of-success upgrade and there is no lane for it — EffectGrant/ItemPassiveEffects only carry numeric bonuses, ranks, senses, IWR, speeds and spells. Ship the two options with no `grant` plus a `note` describing the upgrade; the type comment explicitly sanctions this ("some menus mix a mechanical option with play-time ones … and the pick should still be recorded and shown", as done for kineticist gate junctions).

name: Ancestors' Call
openSource: Pool = common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats. I enumerated it from core.json: 19 level-1 dwarf ancestry feats exist, 10 of them common — the 10 options above. Enumerating is safe here, but the list must be regenerated if dwarf feats are added.
restriction: Common, 1st-level, dwarf, ancestry feats only; three distinct picks; locked in "when you gain this gift".
effect: NOTHING is permanently gained. The three picks are a loadout: on each activation (once per hour) you "Select one of the three ancestry feats" and you plus allies in a 10-foot burst gain that one feat and the dwarf trait for 1 minute. So the build-time job is to record and display the three, not to grant them.
evidence: "When you gain this gift, choose three common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats." … "Select one of the three ancestry feats. You and each ally … gain that feat and the dwarf trait for 1 minute."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) MULTI-PICK: EffectChoice resolves to one value per choice id; three picks would need three sibling choice ids (ancestors-call-1/2/3, with de-duplication between them) or a new multi-pick shape. (2) DISPLAY-ONLY FEAT PICK: the existing feat-picking lane (featPickGrants / FEAT_PICK_GRANTS) permanently grants the chosen feat and tags it "Granted" — using it here would be WRONG, since the character never actually has these feats outside the 1-minute activation. Emit options with no `grant` so the picks are only recorded and shown on the item.

name: Born of Item
openSource: any Lore subject (free text) — the tool/object you used to be
restriction: Flavour-restricted only ("related to what kind of tool you were"); RAW imposes no closed list, so free text is correct.
effect: Trains the character in lore:<typed subject>. ALREADY EXPRESSED: the record carries loreChoices: 1, which build.ts (line ~1208) reads from BuildState.heritageLore and grants as trained, and shared.tsx (~2331) renders as a "Heritage Lore" text input. No new field needed for the training itself.
evidence: "Choose one Lore skill related to what kind of tool you were... You become trained in this skill."
engineNote: The Lore TRAINING works. What does NOT work is the follow-on: "Humanoid Form ... you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Lore skill you obtained through this heritage." FEAT_SITUATIONAL (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts) is keyed by FEAT id only and its SituationalTarget.detail is a static string, so it cannot express (a) a heritage source nor (b) a target resolved from the player's typed Lore. Two gaps: a heritage situational lane, and a dynamic lore:<chosen> target. Yaoguai Humanoid/Yaoguai Form is not modelled anywhere in src (no hits for 'yaoguai' outside two feat grant tables), so the form gate has no home either — display-only is the honest fallback.

name: Warden Human (BB)
restriction: Exactly one of the three; chosen at level 1 and never changes.
effect: hp → +4 flat to maximum HP. fortitude-expert → Fortitude save proficiency raised to expert (RAISES only; a fighter is already expert, so it would be a no-op for them). medium-armor → medium armor proficiency raised to trained.
evidence: "Pick one of the following benefits." — then "Add 4 to your maximum Hit Points", "expert in Fortitude saving throws", "trained in medium armor".
engineNote: Nothing here is expressible today, so this heritage is currently 100% inert. (1) Heritage (types.ts:475) has NO `choice` field — FeatChoiceDef/`choice` lives only on Feat (types.ts:541), and Heritage's mixin DefenseGrants carries senses/resistances/speeds/loreChoices/grantsFeats but no proficiency or HP grants. (2) Even with a choice stored, there is no heritage-side grant lane: save/armor ranks live on FeatGrant (featGrants.ts:58-62) and maxHpBonus lives on Feat (types.ts:562, consumed by featHpBonus in derive.ts:318 which iterates c.feats only) — heritages feed neither. Cheapest path that reuses existing machinery: give Heritage a `choice` + `choiceGrants` pair mirroring FeatGrant.choiceGrants (featGrants.ts:131) and let heritage grants flow through the same apply loop; that also unblocks any other "pick one benefit" heritage. A hackier alternative — three synthetic feats wired via the existing Heritage.grantsFeats — still needs a choice field to pick between them, so it saves nothing.

name: Out-of-Towner
restriction: Closed list of exactly five — the text enumerates them, so any other Lore subject is illegal here.
effect: Trains lore:<picked>. PARTIALLY EXPRESSED: the record sets trainedLoreChoice: true, so build.ts:1203 does train whatever the player types into BuildState.backgroundLore. The training therefore works, but the input is unrestricted free text — a player can type "Dragon Lore" and the app accepts it, which is wrong for this background.
evidence: "a Lore skill thematically associated with the members of the ancestry you grew up with: Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Goblin, or Halfling"
engineNote: Background (types.ts:495) has trainedSkillChoice (a restricted SkillId list) for SKILLS but only a boolean trainedLoreChoice for LORES — there is no way to attach an option list to a Lore choice. Suggested minimal addition: `trainedLoreOptions?: { value: string; label: string }[]`, rendered as a select instead of the free-text input at shared.tsx:2474 when present, and consumed in the same build.ts:1203 branch. The SAME new field is what reputation-seeker needs, so one engine change fixes both.

name: Reputation Seeker
restriction: Closed list of three. RAW the pick also DETERMINES the granted Terrain Expertise terrain: Darklands→underground, Desert→desert, Jungle→forest.
effect: Trains lore:<picked> and should drive the terrain flag of the granted Terrain Expertise feat. CURRENTLY A DATA BUG: the record hardcodes trainedLore: "Jungle" (note also the stray capital J — every other background in this chunk uses a lowercase slug like 'politics', 'orc'), so build.ts:1201 silently trains lore:Jungle and the player is never asked. Two of the three legal builds are unreachable.
evidence: "trained in the Survival skill and the Darklands, Desert, or Jungle Lore skill" — plus "(underground if you have Darklands Lore, desert if you have Desert Lore, or forest if you have Jungle Lore)"
engineNote: Fix is two parts. (1) Drop the hardcoded trainedLore and use the same new `trainedLoreOptions` field proposed for out-of-towner — one engine change covers both records. (2) The coupling to Terrain Expertise is the harder half: feats['terrain-expertise'].choice already exists (flag 'terrain', 9 options incl. underground/desert/forest), but nothing can make a BACKGROUND's lore pick preset or constrain a GRANTED FEAT's choice value. Expressing the coupling needs a new link (e.g. a `derivesFeatChoice?: { featId, flag, map }` on Background).
question: For Reputation Seeker, should the app ENFORCE the printed coupling (Darklands Lore locks Terrain Expertise to underground, Desert→desert, Jungle→forest) — which requires a new background→granted-feat choice link — or should it just offer the 3-option Lore picker and leave the player free to pick any of Terrain Expertise's 9 terrains independently, with a note?

name: Inlander
openSource: any terrain-themed Lore subject (free text) — Hills Lore, Mountains Lore, Swamp Lore, …
restriction: Thematically a terrain type, but the text says "such as", i.e. the examples are illustrative and the list is deliberately OPEN. Free text is the correct model — do NOT convert this one to a closed option list.
effect: Trains lore:<typed subject>. ALREADY FULLY EXPRESSED: the record sets trainedLoreChoice: true, build.ts:1203 slugifies BuildState.backgroundLore and grants it trained, and shared.tsx:2474 renders the input. Nothing to add.
evidence: "a Lore skill related to the terrain type associated with your home region (such as Hills Lore or Mountains Lore)"
engineNote: Contrast with out-of-towner and reputation-seeker in this same chunk: those two enumerate their legal Lores and so need a restricted list; this one says "such as" and must stay free text. name: Fate Tempter's Ring
openSource: any skill (all 16 core skills; Lore subjects the character has, if the app wants to allow them)
restriction: None — the text says only "choose a skill". Locked in when the ring is invested, so it should be re-pickable if the ring is un-invested.
effect: Item bonus to the chosen skill equal to the character's current doomed value. Maps onto ItemPassiveEffects.skills (item bonus to a skill while worn/invested) — except the MAGNITUDE is dynamic, not a constant.

Two honest options: (a) ship the pick now with grant omitted — EffectChoice explicitly permits an option with no grant, and this is numerically CORRECT whenever doomed is 0, which is the normal out-of-combat state; or (b) add a dynamic-value passive lane. Do NOT hardcode a number — that would grant a permanent bonus the character has not earned.
evidence: "When you invest this silver ring, choose a skill; you gain an item bonus to that skill equal to your doomed value."

name: Muse

The text scales the bonus with the relic's level (+2 at 9th, +3 at 17th), and ItemPassiveEffects.skills is a flat number with no level ladder. Either add a level-scaled passive lane or split the gift into three level bands.
evidence: "providing an item bonus to Crafting or Performance checks. (Choose one. If your relic allows you to do so, you can take this gift again to choose the other.) If the relic is 3rd level or higher, you gain a +1 item bonus. Once the relic attains 9th level, the bonus increases to +2. The bonus increases to +3 when the relic is 17th level."

name: Artistic Perfection
restriction: Exactly the two named skills — same pair as the Muse gift, and this record currently has NO effectChoices at all (its sibling aon-muse does).
effect: Any SUCCESS on a check with the chosen skill becomes a critical success.
engineNote: The effect is a degree-of-success upgrade, which no EffectGrant lane can express (skills only carries a proficiency rank; passive only carries numeric bonuses). Minimum viable and honest fix: add the effectChoice with the two options carrying NO grant plus a `note` ("success becomes critical success") — EffectChoice explicitly allows grant-less options so the pick is recorded and displayed. A real implementation needs a degree-of-success-adjustment lane.
evidence: "Your relic enhances your skill with Crafting or Performance. (Choose one.) If you succeed at a check with the chosen skill, you get a critical success instead."

name: Ancestors' Call
openSource: common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats (filter feats by category 'ancestry' + dwarf trait/ancestry + level 1 + rarity common) — do NOT enumerate these inline
restriction: Three DIFFERENT feats; common rarity only; level 1 only; dwarf ancestry feats only. The picks are locked when the gift is gained, so they belong in the builder.
effect: Nothing permanent for the character. At activation, one of the three is selected and granted to the wielder AND every ally in a 10-ft burst, together with the dwarf trait, for 1 minute. The build-time part is only to fix WHICH three are on the menu.
engineNote: Two separate gaps. (1) No feat-picking lane on items: EffectChoice offers `options` and `spellFilter` only — there is no featFilter, and FeatChoiceDef's kinds are 'domains'|'array'. A 3-pick open feat pool is a new lane. (2) The payoff — temporarily granting a feat to the character and to allies — has no representation at all and probably should not have one; the honest scope here is 'record the three names for reference', not 'apply them'. The second, per-activation 'Select one of the three' IS in-play and needs no prompt.
question: Is a 3-pick open feat picker worth building for a single relic gift whose only payoff is a 1-minute temporary grant the engine will not apply anyway? A plain free-text 'note the three feats' field may be the better cost/benefit call — your call as app owner.
evidence: "When you gain this gift, choose three common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats." (vs. the separate in-play step: "Activate Single Action envision; Frequency once per hour; Effect Select one of the three ancestry feats.")

name: Anvil Dwarf
